prs.title: ZIP: The Zcash Town Square
prs.author: emersonian
prs.bodyExcerpt: No ZIP names an official venue for governance discussion. This draft designates the Forum and requires funded organizations to cross-post announcements there. Discussion: https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-the-zcash-town-square/59049

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,607 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: The Zcash Town Square: Official Discussion and Announcement Cross-Posting
+    Owners: Blake Benthall (emersonian) <e@emersonbenthall.com>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-08
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-the-zcash-town-square/59049>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1454>
+    Updates: 1015, 1016
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", and "MAY" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only
+when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Zcash Community Grants" (or "ZCG"), "ZCG Committee", "Financial
+Privacy Foundation" (or "FPF"), "Autonomous Entities", and "Discretionary Budget" in
+this document are to be interpreted as defined in ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015].
+
+The terms "Protocol-defined Ecosystem Funding", "Coinholder-Controlled Fund",
+and "Key-Holder Organizations" in this document are to be interpreted as
+defined in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016], as amended by any later ZIP that updates those
+definitions.
+
+"Zcash Community Forum" (or "the Forum") means the discussion forum hosted at
+<https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/>, or any successor forum designated by a
+ZIP in accordance with [Succession of the Zcash Town Square].
+
+"Zcash Town Square" is the designation given to the Zcash Community Forum by
+this ZIP.
+
+"Other Platform" means any public or semi-public communication channel other
+than the Forum. This includes, but is not limited to: X (formerly Twitter),
+Bluesky, Farcaster, Nostr, Mastodon and other federated networks, Discord,
+Telegram, Signal and WhatsApp groups or channels, Reddit, YouTube, podcasts,
+livestreams, Medium, Substack and other blogs, an organization's own website,
+press releases, newsletters, and GitHub release notes or discussions.
+
+"Zcash Funding Source" means any of the following:
+
+* Protocol-defined Ecosystem Funding, including every Funding Stream
+  [^zip-0207] and Lockbox Funding Stream [^zip-2001] defined by a ZIP;
+* the Zcash Community Grants program, including its Discretionary Budget, as
+  administered by FPF under ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015-zcg] and ZIP 1016;
+* the Coinholder-Controlled Fund, including the ZIP 271 disbursement address
+  [^zip-0271] and any grant approved by a coinholder-amount voting round under
+  ZIP 1016; and
+* any future fund, funding stream, or grant program that is defined, seeded,
+  or authorized by a ZIP.
+
+"Covered Organization" means any of the following, for as long as the
+condition holds and for 12 months afterwards (the "Covered Period"):
+
+* any organization or individual that receives, has received, or is party to
+  an agreement to receive funds from a Zcash Funding Source, whether directly
+  or as a grantee, sub-grantee, or Autonomous Entity;
+* FPF, in its role as administrator of Zcash Community Grants;
+* each Key-Holder Organization; and
+* the ZCG Committee, which is treated as a Covered Organization in its own
+  right, separate from FPF.
+
+An organization that receives payment from a Covered Organization solely as an
+arm's-length vendor of goods or services (for example a hosting provider, an
+auditing firm, or a law firm), and that does not itself receive a grant from a
+Zcash Funding Source, is not a Covered Organization by reason of that payment.
+
+An individual who receives a grant from a Zcash Funding Source in their own
+name, rather than through an organization, is treated as a Covered Organization
+of which they are the sole Executive.
+
+"Executive" means, for a Covered Organization, any natural person who holds
+any of the following roles in that organization:
+
+* chief executive officer, executive director, president, or managing
+  director, or an equivalent head of the organization by any title;
+* any other officer with a title of the form "Chief ... Officer", or an
+  equivalent senior officer;
+* a member of its board of directors, foundation council, or equivalent
+  governing body;
+* a founder or co-founder who continues to hold an operating or governing role;
+* the named lead of any grant from a Zcash Funding Source held by the
+  organization; or
+* for the ZCG Committee, each member of the ZCG Committee.
+
+"Official Account" means any account on an Other Platform that is operated by
+or on behalf of a Covered Organization and that represents itself as speaking
+for that organization, or for a product or project of that organization.
+
+"Covered Speaker" means an Executive of a Covered Organization during its
+Covered Period, or an Official Account of a Covered Organization during its
+Covered Period.
+
+"Announcement" has the meaning given in [Definition of Announcement].
+
+"Official Discussion" has the meaning given in [Official Discussion].
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP affirms that the Zcash Community Forum is the Zcash Town Square: the
+one official venue for discussion of Zcash governance, funding, and protocol
+direction, and the canonical public record of announcements made by
+organizations that are funded by the Zcash community.
+
+It requires every Executive and Official Account of any organization that
+receives funding from a Zcash Funding Source (the ZCG stream, the
+Coinholder-Controlled Fund, or any future ZIP-defined fund), together with the
+Key-Holder Organizations, FPF, and the ZCG Committee, to cross-post to the Forum
+every Announcement they make on any other platform, including but not limited
+to X, within 24 hours. It defines what counts as an Announcement, how a
+cross-post must be made, and how compliance is reported and enforced through
+the grant agreements and disbursement processes that already exist.
+
+This ZIP does not restrict anyone from speaking on any platform. It has limited
+privacy implications, which are discussed in [Privacy Implications]: it does
+not require pseudonymous participants to reveal legal identities.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+Zcash is funded in large part by the Zcash community itself, through block
+subsidies directed to Zcash Community Grants and to the Coinholder-Controlled
+Fund. Organizations that receive those funds are accountable to the community
+that funds them. That accountability depends on the community being able to
+see what those organizations say and decide, in one place, in a durable and
+searchable form.
+
+In practice, important announcements are increasingly made first, and
+sometimes only, on X and other commercial platforms. This creates several
+problems:
+
+* Fragmentation: following what funded organizations have said means
+  watching many accounts on many platforms, some of them invite-only.
+* Access: several platforms require a login to read in full, rate-limit
+  readers, or rank posts so that many interested readers never see them.
+* Durability: posts can be edited, deleted, or lost when an account is
+  suspended or sold, or a platform changes its rules or shuts down, so the
+  record of what an organization committed to can disappear.
+* Discussion: short-form platforms suit careful, threaded debate poorly, and
+  replies scatter across quote-posts that cannot be collected in one place.
+* Capture risk: if the main channel is one commercial platform, its owner
+  gains influence over Zcash governance that the community never granted.
+
+The Forum already plays a central role in Zcash governance. ZIP 0 [^zip-0000]
+directs ZIP authors to post new ideas there and asks Editors to check that
+substantive ZIP updates have been announced there, ZCG grant proposals are discussed
+there, and the questions and results of the NU7 coinholder polls were published
+there [^zip-0259]. However, no ZIP states that the Forum is the official venue,
+and no ZIP requires funded organizations to publish their announcements there.
+This ZIP fills that gap.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+This ZIP does not affect the privacy of Zcash transactions or of Zcash users in
+general.
+
+It requires Covered Organizations to publish a register of their Executives
+and Official Accounts (see [Register of Covered Speakers]). Some Executives,
+particularly of small grantees, participate in Zcash under a pseudonym. The
+register identifies Executives by the public handle under which they already
+act for the organization, and does not require a legal name, address, or any
+other identifying information that the Executive has not already made public.
+
+Cross-posting copies content that a Covered Speaker has already chosen to make
+public. It does not require the publication of private messages, of
+communications within private groups that are not Announcements, or of
+security information that is under responsible-disclosure embargo.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* There is one clearly identified official venue for Zcash governance
+  discussion and for the public record of funded organizations' announcements.
+* Anyone can read that record without an account, and it is archived and
+  searchable.
+* Every Announcement made by an Executive or Official Account of a funded
+  organization on any other platform also appears on the Forum, in full,
+  promptly.
+* The obligation is defined precisely enough that a third party can determine
+  whether a given post is covered and whether it was cross-posted in time.
+* Non-compliance is publicly visible and has proportionate consequences tied
+  to the funding that creates the obligation, using processes that already
+  exist under ZIP 1015 and ZIP 1016.
+* Nothing prevents anyone from using any platform they choose, and the ZIP does
+  not hand new censorship powers to the operator of the Forum.
+* The designation can be moved to a successor venue if the Forum ceases to
+  serve the community.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not regulate what people who are not Covered Speakers say, or
+  where they say it.
+* This ZIP does not regulate the content of Announcements, only where they
+  are published.
+* This ZIP does not move technical review of ZIP text away from the ZIPs
+  repository on GitHub, nor replace synchronous calls such as Arborist calls.
+  It does require that their governance-relevant outcomes be recorded on the
+  Forum.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Designation of the Zcash Town Square
+
+The Zcash Community Forum is designated the Zcash Town Square.
+
+The Zcash Town Square is the sole official venue for Official Discussion, and
+the canonical public record of Announcements made by Covered Speakers.
+
+## Official Discussion
+
+"Official Discussion" means public discussion, proposal, or decision-making
+concerning any of the following:
+
+1. ZIPs, including proposals for new ZIPs and changes to the Status of a ZIP;
+2. network upgrades, including their scope, timing, and activation;
+3. any Zcash Funding Source, including grant proposals, grant decisions,
+   milestone reviews, and disbursements;
+4. coinholder-amount voting rounds and any other community or coinholder
+   polls or votes, including their questions, timing, and results; and
+5. the obligations, conduct, or composition of Covered Organizations insofar
+   as they relate to the matters above.
+
+Discussion of these matters MAY take place on any platform. However:
+
+* Proposals for funding from a Zcash Funding Source MUST be posted on the Forum
+  before they are decided, and the decision MUST be published on the Forum.
+* The questions of every coinholder-amount voting round or other community
+  poll held under a ZIP MUST be published on the Forum before the voting
+  period begins, and the results MUST be published on the Forum.
+* A ZIP's Discussions-To header SHOULD point to a Forum thread. Where it does
+  not, the Owners SHOULD create a Forum thread for the ZIP and link to it from
+  the ZIP.
+* Where a governance-relevant decision or outcome is reached in another venue
+  (for example a call, a GitHub pull request, or a meeting of a Covered
+  Organization), the Covered Organization or ZIP Owner responsible SHOULD post
+  a summary to the Forum within 7 days.
+* A statement made only on an Other Platform has no official standing in any
+  process defined by a ZIP. Any person or body that is required by a ZIP to
+  assess community sentiment or rough consensus SHOULD treat the Forum as the
+  primary record, and SHOULD NOT give weight to statements made only on Other
+  Platforms that were not also posted on the Forum.
+
+## Definition of Announcement
+
+An "Announcement" is a public post, statement, release, or broadcast made by a
+Covered Speaker on an Other Platform that communicates, for the first time on
+that platform, any of the following in relation to Zcash, the Covered
+Organization's Zcash-related work, or Zcash governance:
+
+1. a release, deprecation, or end of support of software, a product, or a
+   service, including wallet and node releases;
+2. a network upgrade, protocol change, or change to a specification;
+3. a security or privacy incident, vulnerability, or risk affecting Zcash users;
+4. funding, grants, revenue, treasury, fundraising, or the receipt or use of
+   funds from any Zcash Funding Source;
+5. a partnership, integration, listing, delisting, or other material
+   relationship with a third party;
+6. a change of leadership, Executives, ownership, name, legal form, or
+   jurisdiction of the Covered Organization, or significant layoffs,
+   restructuring, or wind-down;
+7. a roadmap, plan, or commitment, or a change to or abandonment of one;
+8. a position of the Covered Organization on a ZIP, network upgrade,
+   coinholder-amount voting round, grant proposal, or other governance matter;
+9. a response to a dispute or allegation involving the Covered Organization or
+   any of its Executives in connection with Zcash; or
+10. an event organized or co-organized by the Covered Organization.
+
+For an Executive, a post is an Announcement if it meets the above test and is
+made in, or could reasonably be understood as being made in, their capacity as
+an Executive. A post by an Executive that states a position on a matter listed
+in item 8 is presumed to be made in that capacity unless the post clearly
+states that it is a personal view.
+
+The following are not Announcements:
+
+* replies within an existing conversation that do not communicate any new
+  matter listed above;
+* reposts or quotations of content that has already been posted on the Forum;
+* content that is a translation or restatement of an Announcement that has
+  already been cross-posted, provided that the cross-post is linked;
+* private or direct messages, and messages in private groups that are not
+  public or semi-public channels; and
+* security information that is under a responsible-disclosure embargo, until
+  that embargo ends.
+
+A post in a semi-public channel (such as a Discord or Telegram channel that
+anyone may join) is public for the purposes of this definition.
+
+<details>
+<summary>
+
+### Rationale for the definition of Announcement
+
+</summary>
+
+The definition is written as a list of subject matters, rather than a test of
+importance, so that a third party can apply it without judging how significant
+a post is. Item 8 is included because positions taken by funded organizations
+on governance matters are exactly what the community most needs to see in one
+place, and are most often stated only on X. The presumption that an Executive
+speaks in their official capacity on governance matters prevents the
+obligation from being avoided by speaking "personally" on a matter where the
+Executive's role is the reason their view carries weight; a clear statement
+that a post is personal rebuts it.
+</details>
+
+## Cross-Posting Requirement
+
+Whenever a Covered Speaker makes an Announcement on an Other Platform, the
+Covered Speaker, or the Covered Organization on their behalf, MUST cross-post
+it to the Forum as specified in this section.
+
+### Timing of cross-posts
+
+The cross-post MUST be made within 24 hours of the Announcement first being
+made on any Other Platform. Covered Speakers SHOULD make the cross-post at the
+same time as, or before, the Announcement on Other Platforms.
+
+For an Announcement relating to a security or privacy incident under item 3,
+the cross-post MUST be made within 24 hours of the end of any applicable
+responsible-disclosure embargo, or of the Announcement, whichever is later.
+
+If the same Announcement is made on several Other Platforms, one cross-post is
+sufficient, and it SHOULD link to each of them.
+
+### Content of cross-posts
+
+A cross-post MUST include the full text of the Announcement (every post, for a
+thread), its attachments or working links to them, a link to the original on
+each Other Platform, the name or handle of the Covered Speaker (and, for an
+Executive, their role and organization), and the UTC date and time it was
+first made. A link alone is not a cross-post.
+
+For audio or video, the cross-post MUST include a link to the recording and a
+written summary of each matter announced, and SHOULD include a transcript
+where one exists. For an Announcement not in English, it MUST include the
+original text and SHOULD include an English translation.
+
+A cross-post MUST be made from a Forum account listed for the Covered Speaker
+in the [Register of Covered Speakers], in the Announcements category under
+[Forum Categories], or in a relevant existing thread (such as the thread for a
+ZIP or grant) with a link from the Announcements category.
+
+### Edits and deletions
+
+If an Announcement is materially edited or deleted on an Other Platform, the
+Covered Speaker MUST, within 24 hours, update the cross-post or add a reply to
+it that states what was changed or that the original was deleted. A cross-post
+MUST NOT be deleted, and MUST NOT be edited in a way that removes the original
+text, except where required by law or to remove information whose publication
+would cause harm (such as private keys or personal data published in error);
+in that case the reason MUST be stated in the cross-post.
+
+## Register of Covered Speakers
+
+Each Covered Organization MUST publish on the Forum, and update within 7 days
+of any change, a register of its Executives (by the name or handle under which
+they act for it, with their role), its Official Accounts, and the Forum and
+Other Platform accounts each of them uses for Announcements.
+
+FPF, for ZCG, and the Key-Holder Organizations, for the Coinholder-Controlled
+Fund, MUST each keep on the Forum a list of the Covered Organizations they
+fund, linking to each register.
+
+Nothing in this section requires anyone to disclose their legal name or any
+information they have not already made public.
+
+## Forum Categories
+
+The operator of the Forum is requested to maintain a category for
+Announcements by Covered Speakers (limited to cross-posts and replies), and a
+category or thread for reports of non-compliance under [Enforcement].
+
+If the operator is itself a Covered Organization, it MUST maintain these, MUST
+publish its moderation policy, MUST NOT remove, hide, or edit a cross-post or
+non-compliance report except for spam, illegal content, or doxxing (recording
+each such action and its reason in a public moderation log), and MUST publish
+a downloadable archive of the Announcements category at least quarterly.
+
+## Compliance Reporting
+
+Each Covered Organization that reports quarterly under ZIP 1014 [^zip-1014],
+ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015-transparency], or ZIP 1016 MUST state in each quarterly
+report whether it, its Executives, and its Official Accounts complied with
+this ZIP, describe any non-compliance and how it was remedied, and link to its
+register. Grantees SHOULD include the same statement in milestone reports.
+
+## Enforcement
+
+### Conditions of funding
+
+From the Effective Date, FPF (for ZCG) and the Key-Holder Organizations (for the
+Coinholder-Controlled Fund) MUST include compliance with this ZIP as a condition
+in every grant agreement entered into, renewed, or amended with a Covered
+Organization. Grant agreements in force at the Effective Date SHOULD be amended
+to include it at the earliest opportunity, and in any case MUST include it on
+renewal.
+
+FPF, the ZCG Committee, and the Key-Holder Organizations are themselves bound by
+this ZIP as Covered Organizations, and compliance with it forms part of their
+Transparency and Accountability obligations under ZIP 1015 and ZIP 1016.
+
+### Reporting of non-compliance
+
+Any person MAY report an apparent failure to comply with this ZIP by posting in
+the category or thread designated under [Forum Categories]. A report SHOULD
+include a link to the Announcement and an archived copy of it.
+
+### Notice and cure
+
+When a report is made, or when FPF, the ZCG Committee, or a Key-Holder
+Organization otherwise becomes aware of an apparent failure to comply, the body
+that administers the relevant Zcash Funding Source MUST give the Covered
+Organization notice on the Forum. The Covered Organization has 7 days from the
+notice (the "cure period") to make the missing cross-post or correction, or to
+explain on the Forum why the post in question is not an Announcement.
+
+A failure that is cured within the cure period is a "cured failure". It is
+recorded, but has no further consequence except as set out below.
+
+### Substantial violation
+
+A Covered Organization commits a "substantial violation" of this ZIP if:
+
+* it does not cure a failure within the cure period; or
+* it has three or more cured failures within any period of 12 months.
+
+When a grantee commits a substantial violation:
+
+* FPF and the Key-Holder Organizations, as applicable, MUST suspend any
+  scheduled disbursement to it from the Zcash Funding Source they administer
+  until the violation is cured, and in the case of repeated failures, until
+  30 days have passed with no new failure;
+* for a grant from the Coinholder-Controlled Fund, the Key-Holder Organizations
+  SHOULD treat the violation as a contentious issue for which a further
+  coinholder-amount voting round is held on whether funding should continue,
+  as provided in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016-cc]; and
+* the ZCG Committee, and coinholders in any coinholder-amount voting round,
+  SHOULD take the violation into account in any future funding decision for
+  that Covered Organization.
+
+When FPF, the ZCG Committee, or a Key-Holder Organization commits a substantial
+violation, it constitutes a failure to meet its Transparency and Accountability
+obligations under ZIP 1015 and ZIP 1016, and is subject to the enforcement
+provisions of those ZIPs [^zip-1015-enforcement].
+
+All notices, explanations, cures, suspensions, and resumptions of disbursement
+under this section MUST be published on the Forum.
+
+### Disputes over coverage
+
+If a Covered Organization disputes that a post is an Announcement, the body that
+administers the relevant Zcash Funding Source MUST decide the question and
+publish its decision and reasons on the Forum. Where a Key-Holder Organization
+or FPF is itself the Covered Organization concerned, it MUST NOT take part in
+that decision; the decision is instead made by the remaining Key-Holder
+Organizations, or, for FPF, by the ZCG Committee.
+
+<details>
+<summary>
+
+### Rationale for enforcement through funding
+
+</summary>
+
+A Process ZIP cannot compel anyone to do anything except through the
+obligations and processes that the community already controls. For funded
+organizations, that is the grant agreement and the disbursement schedule.
+Tying the obligation to existing grant agreements and quarterly reports adds
+no new institution, and uses the same enforcement path that ZIP 1015 already
+uses for its Transparency and Accountability obligations.
+
+The notice-and-cure step keeps the consequence proportionate: a missed
+cross-post is easy to fix, and an organization that fixes it promptly loses
+nothing. Only an organization that refuses to fix a failure, or repeatedly
+fails, has disbursements suspended, and even then only until it complies.
+</details>
+
+## Succession of the Zcash Town Square
+
+The designation of the Zcash Town Square may be transferred to a successor
+forum only by a ZIP.
+
+If the Forum becomes unavailable for more than 7 consecutive days, Covered
+Speakers MUST, for as long as it remains unavailable, publish cross-posts on
+their own website or in a public GitHub repository, and MUST additionally
+cross-post them to the Forum within 7 days after it becomes available again.
+
+## Effective Date
+
+This ZIP takes effect 30 days after its Status becomes Active (the "Effective
+Date"). Covered Organizations MUST publish their registers within 30 days after
+the Effective Date. Announcements made before the Effective Date are not
+covered, but Covered Speakers are encouraged to comply voluntarily from the
+time this ZIP becomes Active.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Why the Forum
+
+The Forum is already the venue that ZIP 0 and the funding ZIPs rely on in
+practice. It is readable without an account, its threads are durable and
+searchable, it supports long-form, threaded discussion, and it is not operated
+for the purpose of maximizing engagement. Designating it formally makes the
+existing practice explicit and gives the community one place to check.
+
+## Why cross-posting rather than exclusivity
+
+Reaching people where they are is important for Zcash adoption, and requiring
+funded organizations to stop using X or other platforms would be both
+unenforceable and harmful. Cross-posting preserves outreach on every platform
+while ensuring that the Forum holds a complete record. Covered Speakers are
+encouraged, but not required, to post on the Forum first.
+
+## Why 24 hours
+
+A short window keeps the Forum record current enough to be useful for
+discussion of the Announcement, while allowing for time zones and for
+Announcements made outside working hours. A longer window would allow
+discussion to form elsewhere before the Forum sees the Announcement.
+
+## Why Executives and Official Accounts
+
+This ZIP covers the Executives of funded organizations because they speak
+for those organizations. Official Accounts
+are added because organizations most often announce through their own brand
+accounts, and leaving them out would leave the largest source of
+announcements uncovered. Ordinary employees and contributors are not covered,
+to keep the obligation focused and administrable.
+
+## Why the Key-Holder Organizations, FPF, and ZCG Committee are covered
+
+These bodies administer Zcash Funding Sources on the community's behalf.
+Their Announcements about funding and governance are at least as important to
+the community as those of grantees, and they are covered whether or not they
+themselves receive grants.
+
+## Why include an obligation on the Forum operator
+
+Designating one venue as official gives its operator influence over what is
+seen. If the operator is a Covered Organization, the moderation-log, archive,
+and non-removal requirements limit the risk that this influence is used to
+suppress Announcements or reports of non-compliance. The Succession section
+lets the community move the designation if the Forum ceases to serve it.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+* A voluntary norm: already the informal expectation; it has not prevented
+  announcements being made only on X.
+* Requiring Forum-first publication: stronger, but harder to verify and
+  more disruptive to coordinated launches with partners. It is recommended
+  instead of required.
+* Covering only Official Accounts: would miss governance positions stated
+  by Executives personally, which is the case this ZIP most needs to cover.
+* A de minimis exemption for small grants: not included in this draft,
+  so that the rule matches its stated scope of "any organization that receives
+  funding". See [Open questions].
+
+## Open questions
+
+The following questions are left open for discussion while this ZIP is a
+Draft:
+
+* Should individual grantees, or grants below some threshold, be exempt or
+  subject to a lighter obligation?
+* Should grants made by Covered Organizations from their own reserves (for
+  example reserves originally derived from the earlier Dev Fund under ZIP 1014)
+  be treated as a Zcash Funding Source?
+* Is 12 months the right length for the Covered Period after funding ends?
+* Should ZIP Editors, in their role as Editors, be asked to post decisions on
+  ZIP Status changes to the Forum? This would require an update to ZIP 0.
+
+

prs.title: Add draft ZIP for coinholder elections to Zcash Community Grants
prs.author: thowar2
prs.bodyExcerpt: ZCG committee members are currently selected through ZCAP elections. This draft proposes electing them through private, ZEC-weighted approval voting under ZIPs 1015 and 1016. It retains the staggered committee terms and uses the existing coinholder participation threshold for the election as a whole

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,375 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Coinholder Elections for Zcash Community Grants
+    Owners: Tom Howard <tom@zcashlabs.org>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Consensus Process
+    Created: 2026-10-29
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/proposal-to-switch-zcg-elections-to-token-holder-voting/53533>
+    Updates: 1015, 1016
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHALL", and "SHOULD" in this document
+are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when,
+they appear in all capitals.
+
+"Zcash Community Grants" ("ZCG"), "ZCG Committee", "Zcash Community Advisory
+Panel" ("ZCAP"), and "Financial Privacy Foundation" ("FPF") have the meanings
+given in ZIP 1015, subject to the amendment to ZCG's definition below.
+[^zip-1015]
+
+"Coinholder-Controlled Fund" ("CCF") has the meaning given in ZIP 1016.
+[^zip-1016] "ZEC" is the native currency of Zcash Mainnet.
+
+"Coinholder election" means an election in which eligible ZEC provides voting
+weight, rather than membership in ZCAP. "Approval voting" means that a voter
+can support any number of candidates and the candidates with the highest
+approval totals fill the available seats, subject to committee eligibility
+constraints.
+
+"Effective Date" means the UTC date specified for the transition under
+[Activation and transition]. This date is unassigned in this draft.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP changes the electorate that selects the Zcash Community Grants
+Committee. ZEC holders would elect committee members through private,
+ZEC-weighted approval voting, replacing elections by the Zcash Community
+Advisory Panel. The committee would continue to evaluate and approve grants
+under its existing mandate.
+
+The proposal preserves the five-seat committee, staggered elections, one-year
+terms, eligibility for reelection, conflict-of-interest rules, and existing
+candidate nomination process. It changes neither ZCG's funding allocation nor
+the use of its treasury. FPF would continue administering the program under
+the existing financial, legal, and reporting constraints. ZCAP's separate
+roles in determining the Discretionary Budget and committee compensation
+would remain unchanged.
+
+This ZIP specifies amendments to ZIPs 1015 and 1016 and requires corresponding
+amendments to FPF's legal commitments so that the election results govern
+committee selection under the program's binding arrangements. Publication or
+adoption of a ZIP alone does not amend an existing agreement.
+
+The voting mechanism is outside the scope of this proposal. The remaining
+election rules and rollout details are to be completed before activation.
+It introduces no changes to Zcash consensus rules or transaction privacy.
+Election privacy nevertheless depends on the voting system, its operators,
+and the information exposed during participation and tallying.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 1015 provides for a five-seat ZCG Committee selected by ZCAP or a successor
+process. ZIP 1016 continues this arrangement while providing a separate
+coinholder-directed funding channel. [^zip-1015-zcg] [^zip-1016]
+
+In the June 2026 ZCG election, ZCAP used approval voting to fill two seats.
+Voters could approve multiple candidates, and the two candidates with the
+most approvals were elected. [^zcg-june-2026] This gives members of an advisory
+panel the formal role of selecting the committee, while ZEC ownership alone
+provides no participation right in that election.
+
+ZEC holders have an economic interest in the long-term effects of development
+funding. Giving them responsibility for electing ZCG members would connect
+that interest to the selection of the people who allocate ZCG resources. It
+would also allow participation without admission to a membership panel. The
+proposal retains a representative committee, allowing holders to choose its
+members without requiring a coinholder vote on each ZCG grant.
+
+ZIP 1016 leaves the definition of the coinholder voting model to a separate
+ZIP. [^zip-1016] No Active ZIP currently specifies a coinholder voting
+mechanism for these elections. This proposal defines the election rules and
+leaves the voting technology to separate work.
+
+The change is deliberately limited to committee selection. It does not
+transfer ZCG's grant decisions to the CCF or change the committee's duties,
+budget authority, or FPF's administration of grants.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+ZEC-weighted voting can expose financial information if eligibility proofs or
+ballots reveal balances, addresses, or links between holdings and choices.
+This proposal calls for private ballots and independently verifiable aggregate
+results. How the voting system protects individual balances and choices
+depends on its design and operational assumptions.
+
+Small participation sets, distinctive voting weights, repeated elections, and
+network metadata can still create inference or correlation risks. A private
+ballot also does not by itself establish resistance to coercion or vote
+buying. These risks need independent review in the context of the voting
+system used for ZCG elections.
+
+Candidates would continue to participate through the existing nomination and
+disclosure process. This ZIP does not alter Zcash transaction formats,
+shielded payment privacy, or the information grantees provide to FPF.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* Replace ZCAP membership with eligible ZEC as the basis for voting in ZCG
+  committee elections, using private, verifiable coinholder voting.
+* Preserve approval voting and the existing committee structure, nomination
+  process, election cadence, term lengths, and eligibility constraints.
+* Preserve ZCG's grant mandate, funding, treasury, administration, and all
+  governance responsibilities other than the election of committee members.
+* Make the election outcome binding on FPF through explicit amendments to
+  ZIPs 1015 and 1016 and the corresponding legal commitments.
+* Protect voter balances and choices while allowing independent verification
+  of the tally and its application to the available seats.
+* Transition prospectively, without shortening or extending existing terms
+  or reopening completed elections.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+The following requirements govern ZCG committee selection and its legal
+implementation. They do not change Zcash consensus rules.
+
+## Electorate and ballot
+
+From the Effective Date, ZCG Committee members MUST be selected by coinholder
+election instead of a ZCAP election or another membership-panel election.
+FPF MUST arrange the election, with technical and administrative support
+as needed. ZCAP membership MUST NOT be a condition of voter eligibility.
+Any individual or organization controlling eligible ZEC MUST be permitted
+to vote; the association limits on committee members do not restrict voters.
+
+Elections MUST use ZEC-weighted approval voting. For each candidate, the
+ballot MUST allow approval or non-approval. A voter MUST be permitted to
+approve any number of candidates, including none. The same eligible voting
+weight MUST be usable independently for each candidate; it MUST NOT be
+divided by the number of candidates approved.
+
+Each candidate's score is the sum of the valid ZEC voting weight approving
+that candidate. In an election that meets quorum, available seats MUST be
+filled in descending order of score, subject to the eligibility and
+association limits in point 7 of ZIP 1015's "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)"
+section, including associations of members whose terms continue. Approval of
+a candidate does not require a separate majority of the participating weight.
+
+An election MUST meet the minimum ZEC participation threshold in force for
+CCF grant votes under ZIP 1016 when voting opens. [^zip-1016] Turnout is the
+total eligible ZEC represented by valid ballots. The same ZEC MUST be counted
+only once toward turnout, regardless of how many candidates it approves.
+An election that falls short of quorum MUST NOT fill any seats.
+
+## Election administration and record
+
+Elections MUST protect individual choices and balances and allow independent
+verification of the aggregate tally. Elections MUST follow any applicable
+Active ZIPs governing ZEC eligibility, voting weight, ballot validation,
+or tally verification.
+
+When FPF opens nominations, it MUST announce the voting window, number of
+seats, and candidate eligibility rules. FPF MUST publish the voter
+eligibility rules and voting instructions in time for
+voters to prepare before any eligibility cutoff and participate in the vote.
+The final candidate list and its mapping to the ballot MUST be published
+before voting opens. The election record MUST include the quorum threshold,
+turnout, and verified aggregate tally. It MUST explain how the quorum and
+candidate eligibility rules determined the outcome.
+
+Tie resolution and procedures for an invalid or interrupted election or an
+election that falls short of quorum remain open in this draft. These rules
+MUST be resolved in this ZIP before it becomes Active, including how
+vacancies are handled without changing the existing one-year terms or
+granting FPF discretion to appoint unelected candidates.
+
+## Activation and transition
+
+This ZIP MUST NOT take effect while its status is Draft. Before activation,
+the ZIP process MUST establish community adoption, this ZIP MUST specify an
+Effective Date, and FPF MUST publish confirmation that the legal requirements
+below have been satisfied.
+
+The new electorate MUST apply to elections whose nomination period opens on
+or after the Effective Date, including elections to fill vacancies. An
+election already underway before that date MUST finish under its announced
+rules. Completed elections and the terms of sitting members are unaffected.
+
+The five-seat committee, staggered election schedule, one-year terms,
+eligibility for reelection, candidate nomination process, conflict-of-interest
+requirements, and association limits MUST continue. Except for replacing the
+electorate and implementing coin weighting and ballot privacy as specified
+here, existing election procedures MUST continue.
+
+This is a change to a community process. Activation does not require a network
+upgrade or changes to ZIP 214's funding-stream definitions. A rehearsal
+SHOULD be held before the first election. Rehearsals MUST NOT select ZCG
+Committee members or confer authority over ZCG funds.
+
+## Legal implementation by FPF
+
+FPF MUST arrange amendments, in suitable legal language, to the restricted-fund
+agreements and other binding commitments through which it implements ZIPs
+1015 and 1016. The amendments MUST require FPF to recognize the candidates
+elected under this ZIP as the ZCG Committee members for the relevant seats
+and terms, subject to the existing eligibility requirements and applicable
+law. A separate ZCAP ratification MUST NOT be required.
+
+Before the Effective Date, FPF MUST obtain advice from qualified Cayman
+Islands counsel on the necessary amendments, consents, and corporate
+approvals, and complete those steps. The binding instruments MUST identify
+the parties entitled to enforce the election obligations and the applicable
+enforcement procedure. This ZIP does not itself confer legal standing on
+every ZEC holder or automatically amend an agreement or FPF's constitutional
+documents.
+
+FPF MUST publish confirmation of the completed legal arrangements and their
+effect on committee selection, protecting privileged advice and confidential
+information. If a necessary authorization cannot be obtained, FPF MUST report
+the obstacle and the transition MUST be deferred pending its resolution.
+Existing arrangements continue in the meantime; this does not authorize FPF
+to replace elections with discretionary appointments.
+
+## Changes to ZIP 1015
+
+In "Terminology", replace the definition of "Zcash Community Grants" with:
+
+> "Zcash Community Grants", also called "ZCG", refers to the committee
+> selected under the ZIP "Coinholder Elections for Zcash Community Grants"
+> to decide on the funding of grants intended to fund the Zcash ecosystem.
+
+In "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)", replace point 5 with:
+
+> 5. ZCG awards are subject to approval by a five-seat ZCG Committee. From the
+>    Effective Date, the ZCG Committee SHALL be selected by ZEC-weighted
+>    coinholder approval voting under the ZIP "Coinholder Elections for Zcash
+>    Community Grants", subject to its transition rules. Elections SHALL be
+>    staggered to ensure continuity within the Committee.
+
+Immediately after the paragraph requiring FPF to recognize the ZCG slice as
+a Restricted Fund donation, insert:
+
+> The contractual constraints on the ZCG Restricted Fund MUST include FPF's
+> obligation to implement committee selection under the ZIP "Coinholder
+> Elections for Zcash Community Grants". FPF MUST arrange the corresponding
+> legal amendments and approvals before that ZIP's Effective Date. All other
+> restrictions on the use and administration of ZCG funds continue in effect.
+> These commitments remain subject to the Enforcement section of this ZIP.
+
+Add references to this ZIP at those amendments and in the References section,
+using its assigned identifier when available. These amendments take effect
+under [Activation and transition]. Points 8 and 9, including ZCAP's or its
+successor process's roles in determining the Discretionary Budget and member
+compensation, MUST remain unchanged. Coinholder elections MUST NOT be
+interpreted as replacing those separate roles.
+
+## Changes to ZIP 1016
+
+In "Non-requirements", replace the first bullet with:
+
+> * Changes to ZCG or its governance, other than the committee-election
+>   amendments specified in the ZIP "Coinholder Elections for Zcash Community
+>   Grants", remain outside this proposal's scope.
+
+In "Zcash Community Grants", append to the first paragraph:
+
+> Those rules include the amendments to ZIP 1015 specified in the ZIP
+> "Coinholder Elections for Zcash Community Grants", effective according to
+> that ZIP's activation and transition provisions.
+
+In "Administrative obligations and constraints", append to the first
+paragraph:
+
+> FPF MUST implement the committee-election amendments in the ZIP "Coinholder
+> Elections for Zcash Community Grants", including the corresponding changes
+> to its legally binding commitments governing ZCG funds.
+
+After the paragraph that applies ZCG provisions to the Key-Holder
+Organizations' administration of the CCF, insert:
+
+> The committee-election amendments specified in the ZIP "Coinholder
+> Elections for Zcash Community Grants" apply only to selection of ZCG
+> Committee members and FPF's implementation of that selection. They do not
+> change the Coinholder-Controlled Fund's Key-Holder Organizations, grant
+> approval rules, voting thresholds, veto process, or legal arrangements.
+
+Add references to this ZIP at those insertions and in the References section,
+using its assigned identifier when available. All other provisions of ZIP
+1016 continue in effect.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Retaining a grants committee
+
+Coinholder elections retain ZCG's existing division of work: an elected
+committee evaluates applications, and FPF administers the program. Direct
+coinholder voting on individual ZCG grants would be a broader redesign and
+would duplicate aspects of the CCF. This proposal changes who chooses the
+representatives while preserving what those representatives do.
+
+## Preserving approval voting
+
+Approval voting is already used for ZCG elections. [^zcg-december-2025]
+Weighting approvals by ZEC preserves the ability to support multiple
+candidates without splitting voting weight among them. The CCF's minimum
+participation threshold applies to the election as a whole. Once quorum is
+met, the approval totals determine the order in which candidates fill seats.
+
+FPF published the June 2026 voting window when it opened nominations.
+[^zcg-june-2026-nominations] The same practice fits the staggered election
+calendar and gives FPF room to accommodate any voter eligibility cutoff.
+
+## Concentration and participation
+
+Coin weighting gives larger holders more influence, and a sufficiently large
+participating holder could determine all seats being contested. It does not
+provide one-person-one-vote representation or guarantee decentralization.
+Depending on the voting rules, temporarily borrowed balances can count and
+custodians may vote without reflecting each beneficial owner's preference.
+These are tradeoffs of the proposed electorate, not problems eliminated by
+ballot privacy. Public nominations, staggered terms, and existing committee
+constraints remain useful but do not remove those risks.
+
+The applicable voting rules can limit which holdings qualify and how voters
+prepare to participate. Adequate notice matters to participation. Quorum and
+failure rules need to balance legitimacy against the risk of leaving seats
+unfilled.
+
+## Express amendments and legal commitments
+
+ZIP 1015 already permits a successor selection process, but leaves ZCAP
+selection as an option. An express amendment makes the replacement electorate
+unambiguous. Updating ZIP 1016 ensures that its continuation of ZIP 1015's
+obligations carries the same rule forward.
+
+The legal arrangements are necessary to make FPF's obligation executable
+under the restricted-fund framework. The proposal retains the existing
+Enforcement provision; it does not implement automatic on-chain enforcement
+or alter funding streams. The distinction between process adoption and
+contractual implementation is essential to the intended binding effect.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* How are tied scores at the seat boundary, zero-support candidates,
+  insufficient eligible candidates, and elections that are interrupted or
+  fall short of quorum handled while preserving the existing terms and cadence?
+* Which FPF agreements and corporate instruments need amendment, whose
+  consent is required, and who can enforce the revised election obligations?
+* What Effective Date allows the legal work, independent security and privacy
+  review, wallet preparation, and rehearsal to finish before nominations open?
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14 — RFC 2119 and RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^zip-1015]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding](zip-1015.rst)
+
+[^zip-1015-zcg]: [ZIP 1015: Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)](zip-1015.rst#zcash-community-grants-zcg)
+
+[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](zip-1016.md)
+
+[^zcg-june-2026]: [Zcash Foundation: ZCAP Poll Now Open — ZCG Election, June 2026](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zcap-poll-now-open-zcg-election-june-2026/56156)
+
+[^zcg-june-2026-nominations]: [FPF: Zcash Community Grants Nominations Now Open for June Election](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zcash-community-grants-zcg-nominations-now-open-for-june-election/55720)
+
+[^zcg-december-2025]: [FPF: ZCAP SIV Poll — ZCG Elections, December 2025](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zcap-siv-poll-zcg-elections-open-now/53685)

prs.title: Draft ZIP: Expand the ZCG Committee to Seven Seats
prs.author: emersonian
prs.bodyExcerpt: ZIP 1016 left expansion of the ZCG Committee out of scope. ZCG now manages a significantly larger budget than it was originally designed to steward. This draft adds two seats filled by the existing selection process, sets a quorum, and requires at least four votes in favor for grants over US$500,000

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,316 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Update to ZIP 1015: Expand the ZCG Committee to Seven Seats
+    Owners: Blake Benthall (emersonian) <e@emersonbenthall.com>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-08
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-expand-zcg-to-seven-seats-adjust-limits/59047>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1452>
+    Updates: 1015
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHALL", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document
+are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they
+appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Zcash Community Grants" (or "ZCG"), "ZCG Committee", "Financial
+Privacy Foundation" (or "FPF"), "Zcash Community Advisory Panel" (or "ZCAP"),
+and "Discretionary Budget" in this document are to be interpreted as defined or
+used in ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015].
+
+The terms "Bootstrap Project" (or "BP"), "Electric Coin Company" (or "ECC"), and
+"Zcash Foundation" (or "ZF") in this document are to be interpreted as used in
+ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015].
+
+"Zcash Open Development Lab" (or "ZODL") refers to Znewco, Inc., the company
+formed in 2026 by the former engineering and product team of ECC
+[^draft-mcgee-keyholders]. ZODL is a separate organization from ECC.
+
+The term "Key-Holder Organizations" in this document is to be interpreted as
+described in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016], as amended by any ZIP that updates their
+membership (see for example [^draft-mcgee-keyholders]).
+
+"ZEC" refers to the native currency of Zcash on Mainnet.
+
+The terms below are to be interpreted as follows:
+
+Member
+
+: A person who holds a seat on the ZCG Committee.
+
+Seated Members
+
+: The Members holding a seat at a given time. A seat that is vacant is not
+  counted.
+
+Large Grant
+
+: A grant, or an extension, renewal, or increase of a grant, whose total value
+  over its full term is more than US$500,000, valued at the time of the
+  decision. Grants to the same applicant for closely related work approved
+  within a 90-day period are added together for this purpose.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP increases the ZCG Committee from five seats to seven.
+
+The two new seats are filled by the same process that selects the existing
+seats, in the next selection round after this ZIP becomes Active, and are
+placed in the election cycles so that four seats and three seats come up for
+selection at different times. The association limits in ZIP 1015 are extended to ZODL
+and to the Key-Holder Organizations, and at most three Members in total may
+have any of those associations, so that at least four Members have none.
+
+The ZIP also sets a quorum of five Members, and requires at least four votes in
+favor for any Large Grant, so that a decision worth more than US$500,000 is
+always backed by a majority of the full Committee.
+
+Committee compensation continues to be set by ZCAP and paid from the
+Discretionary Budget. The ZIP has no significant privacy implications.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 1015 provides that "ZCG awards are subject to approval by a five-seat ZCG
+Committee" [^zip-1015-zcg]. That size was carried over from the Major Grants
+committee of ZIP 1014 [^zip-1014], when the amounts involved were much smaller
+and ZCG's role was narrower. ZIP 1016 recognized this, noting that "Any
+changes to the ZCG or its governance, such as its expansion to include more
+members, may be desired but are specifically outside this proposal's scope"
+[^zip-1016].
+
+The ZCG funding stream is 8% of the block subsidy. At the current issuance
+rate that is about 144 ZEC per day, or roughly 52,500 ZEC a year (8% of
+1.5625 ZEC per 75-second block, or the equivalent at 25-second spacing). At
+recent prices this is on the order of US$60 million a year, decided by five
+people. These figures are the author's arithmetic and are given for scale only.
+
+A five-seat Committee has several weaknesses at that scale:
+
+* Recusal removes a large share of the Committee. ZIP 1015 requires Members to
+  recuse when they have a financial interest. One recusal leaves four people,
+  and two leave three, so a single conflicted decision can rest on a bare
+  majority of a much smaller group.
+* The association limits leave little room for independence. ZIP 1015 allows
+  at most one Member associated with each of BP/ECC, ZF, and FPF
+  [^zip-1015-zcg]. On a five-seat Committee, those three seats can form a
+  majority on their own. ZIP 1015 also says nothing about ZODL, which did not
+  exist when it was written, or about the Key-Holder Organizations, which
+  administer the Coinholder-Controlled Fund.
+* A majority is easy to reach. Three people decide any question, and three
+  people are a small target for pressure from applicants or other interests.
+* Workload is concentrated. Five people review every grant, monitor
+  milestones, and approve Discretionary Budget spending, which limits how
+  carefully each application can be read.
+
+Seven seats address these without changing how the Committee is selected or
+what it does.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+This ZIP has no significant privacy implications. It changes the number of
+seats on an existing public committee and its voting rules. The new Members
+are selected and disclosed in the same way as current Members.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* The ZCG Committee has seven seats.
+* The new seats are filled by the existing selection process, without
+  interrupting the Committee's work.
+* Seats continue to come up for selection on a staggered schedule.
+* Once the new seats are filled, at least four Members have no association
+  with BP/ECC, ZODL, ZF, FPF, or any Key-Holder Organization.
+* Once the new seats are filled, decisions are normally made by at least five
+  Members and never by fewer than four, and no Large Grant is approved with
+  fewer than four votes in favor.
+* The cost of the larger Committee stays within the existing Discretionary
+  Budget process.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not change who selects the ZCG Committee, the one-year term,
+  or the conflict-of-interest policy in ZIP 1015.
+* This ZIP does not add a procedure for removing Members or filling
+  mid-term vacancies. Those are left to other proposals.
+* This ZIP does not change the ZCG funding stream or the uses of ZCG funds.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Number of seats
+
+In item 5 of the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015
+[^zip-1015-zcg], "a five-seat ZCG Committee" is replaced with "a seven-seat ZCG
+Committee".
+
+## Association limits
+
+In item 7 of the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015
+[^zip-1015-zcg], the sentence beginning "At most one person with association
+with the BP/ECC" is replaced with:
+
+> At most one person with association with the BP/ECC or ZODL, at most one
+> person with association with the ZF, at most one person with association with
+> FPF, and at most one person with association with each other Key-Holder
+> Organization are allowed to sit on the ZCG Committee. In total, at most three
+> Members may have an association with any of these organizations, so that at
+> least four Members of a seven-seat Committee have none.
+
+The definition of "Association" in that item applies to each of these
+organizations.
+
+These limits apply to selections made after this ZIP becomes Active. A Member
+already seated when this ZIP becomes Active MAY serve out their current term.
+
+## Filling the new seats
+
+The two new seats SHALL be filled by the ZF's Community Advisory Panel or
+successor process, in the same way as the existing seats, at the first
+selection round that opens at least 30 days after this ZIP becomes Active.
+If no selection round is scheduled within 90 days after this ZIP becomes
+Active, the selecting body SHOULD hold a special round for the new seats
+within that period.
+
+To keep elections staggered, the selecting body SHALL assign the seven seats
+to two groups, one of four seats and one of three, whose selection rounds are
+held at different times of the year. Where this requires one of the new seats
+to be filled for a first term shorter or longer than one year, that first term
+MAY be adjusted by up to six months. Every later term is one year, as in item
+7 of the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015.
+
+The selecting body SHALL publish the assignment of seats to groups, and the
+dates of each group's selection round, on the Zcash Community Forum before the
+new seats are filled.
+
+Until the new seats are filled, the ZCG Committee continues to operate with
+its existing Members, and the quorum and voting rules in this ZIP apply with
+five in place of seven seats: the quorum is four, and a Large Grant requires
+three votes in favor.
+
+## Quorum and voting
+
+A decision of the ZCG Committee MUST NOT be made unless at least five Members
+who are not recused take part.
+
+A decision is approved by a majority of the votes cast by Members who are not
+recused.
+
+A Large Grant MUST NOT be approved unless at least four Members vote in favor.
+
+If recusals or vacancies mean that fewer than five Members are able to take
+part in a decision, the decision MAY be made by all Members who are able to
+take part, provided that there are at least four of them, and provided that a
+Large Grant still receives at least four votes in favor. The ZCG Committee
+MUST record in its published minutes when a decision is made under this
+paragraph, and why.
+
+The ZCG Committee MUST publish, for each grant decision, the number of Members
+who voted in favor, against, and abstained, and the number who recused.
+
+## Compensation
+
+Compensation for the new seats SHALL be determined by ZCAP or successor
+process, and paid from the Discretionary Budget, under item 9 of the section
+"Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015, in the same way as for the
+existing seats. ZCAP SHOULD review the size of the Discretionary Budget to
+take account of the additional seats.
+
+## Changes to ZIP 1015
+
+In the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015-zcg]:
+
+* in item 5, "a five-seat ZCG Committee" is replaced with "a seven-seat ZCG
+  Committee";
+* in item 7, the sentence on associations is replaced as specified in
+  [Association limits](#association-limits); and
+* at the end of item 5, the following is added:
+
+> The ZCG Committee's quorum, voting rules, and the transition from five to
+> seven seats are specified in ZIP [this ZIP].
+
+## Effective date
+
+This ZIP takes effect on the date its Status becomes Active.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Why seven
+
+Seven is the smallest odd number that leaves a clear independent majority
+under the association limits in this ZIP: with at most three associated
+Members, at least four are independent. It also means that one recusal still
+leaves six Members, and two leave five, so a quorum can almost always be met.
+
+Larger committees, such as nine or eleven, would further reduce the weight of
+each Member, but would be harder to fill with qualified people each year, cost
+more, and make discussion slower.
+
+## Why extend the association limits
+
+The limits in ZIP 1015 name BP/ECC, ZF, and FPF. Since then, ECC's former team
+has formed ZODL, and the Key-Holder Organizations have taken on administration
+of the Coinholder-Controlled Fund. ZODL shares the BP/ECC limit because its
+people were the ECC team when that limit was written. Adding organizations one
+at a time would erode the independent majority, so the total is capped at
+three.
+
+## Why a four-vote floor for Large Grants
+
+Under a simple majority of those voting, a Large Grant could pass with three
+votes if several Members were recused or absent. Requiring four votes means
+that every large decision is backed by a majority of the full Committee. The
+US$500,000 threshold is meant to catch the grants that matter most to ZCG's
+budget while leaving routine grants unaffected.
+
+## Why keep the existing selection process
+
+How the Committee is selected is a separate and more contested question. This
+ZIP only changes its size, so that it can be adopted without settling that
+question. It works with any selection process that ZIP 1015 or a later ZIP
+specifies.
+
+## Relationship to other drafts
+
+This ZIP fits with the drafts that bar Members from applying for grants during
+their term [^draft-grant-bar] and that move treasury decisions to a separate
+Treasury Committee [^draft-zcg-treasury]. Neither depends on this one. If the
+Treasury Committee draft is adopted, the grants committee will spend its time
+on grant review, which makes the extra seats more useful.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* Is US$500,000 the right threshold for a Large Grant, and should it be set in
+  ZEC instead?
+* Should the quorum be five, or a majority of Seated Members?
+* Should the new seats be reserved, at least initially, for people with no
+  association with BP/ECC, ZODL, ZF, FPF, a Key-Holder Organization, or any
+  current grantee?
+* Should this ZIP also add a rule for filling a mid-term vacancy?
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14, "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^zip-1014]: [ZIP 1014: Establishing a Dev Fund for ECC, ZF, and Major Grants](zip-1014.rst)
+
+[^zip-1015]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding](zip-1015.rst)
+
+[^zip-1015-zcg]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding, Zcash Community Grants](zip-1015.rst#zcash-community-grants-zcg)
+
+[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](zip-1016.md)
+
+[^draft-mcgee-keyholders]: [Draft ZIP: Update to ZIP 1016 & ZIP 271: Key-Holder Organizations](draft-mcgee-keyholders-organizations.md)
+
+[^draft-grant-bar]: Draft ZIP: Update to ZIP 1015: ZCG Committee Members May Not Apply for Grants During Their Term (separate draft)
+
+[^draft-zcg-treasury]: Draft ZIP: ZCG Treasury Committee, Budget, and Hedging Plan (separate draft)

prs.title: Draft ZIP: Restriction of ZCG Member Grant Applications
prs.author: emersonian
prs.bodyExcerpt: ZIP 1015 requires recusal but does not stop a sitting member from applying to the committee they serve on. This draft bars applications during a member's term. Discussion: https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-restriction-of-zcg-member-grant-applications/59046

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,324 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Update to ZIP 1015: ZCG Committee Members May Not Apply for Grants During Their Term
+    Owners: Blake Benthall (emersonian) <e@emersonbenthall.com>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-08
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-restriction-of-zcg-member-grant-applications/59046>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1451>
+    Updates: 1015, 1016
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document are to
+be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Zcash Community Grants" (or "ZCG"), "ZCG Committee", "Financial
+Privacy Foundation" (or "FPF"), "Autonomous Entities", and "Discretionary Budget" in
+this document are to be interpreted as defined or used in ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015].
+
+The term "Coinholder-Controlled Fund" in this document is to be interpreted as
+described in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016].
+
+The terms below are to be interpreted as follows:
+
+Member
+
+: A person who holds a seat on the ZCG Committee, whether elected, appointed,
+  or filling a vacancy.
+
+Term
+
+: The period from the time a person becomes a Member until the time they stop
+  being a Member, for any reason. Consecutive terms, including a term that
+  follows reelection, are treated as one continuous Term.
+
+ZCG Grant
+
+: Any grant, contract, bounty, retroactive award, or other payment approved by
+  the ZCG Committee and paid from funds administered by FPF for Zcash Community
+  Grants. This includes an extension, renewal, increase, or new milestone of an
+  existing grant. It does not include payments from the Discretionary Budget
+  described in [Permitted payments to Members](#permitted-payments-to-members).
+
+Associated Applicant
+
+: For a given Member, any of the following:
+
+  1. the Member;
+  2. any organization of which the Member is an officer, director, or
+     full-time employee, or in which the Member has a financial interest; and
+  3. any immediate family member of the Member, or any organization associated
+     with an immediate family member in the way described in item 2.
+
+  "Financial interest" and "immediate family relationship" have the same
+  meaning as in the definition of "Association" in ZIP 1015, item 7 of the
+  section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" [^zip-1015-zcg].
+
+Application
+
+: A request for a ZCG Grant, by whatever name or method it is made, including
+  a response to a request for proposals and a request made on someone's behalf.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP bars members of the ZCG Committee from applying for, or receiving,
+Zcash Community Grants while they sit on the Committee. The bar covers the
+member personally, organizations they lead, work for full-time, or have a
+financial interest in, and their immediate family. It also covers being named
+on someone else's application as a team member, contractor, or other paid
+participant.
+
+Grants that a member already held before taking their seat may continue on
+their existing terms, but cannot be extended, renewed, or increased during the
+member's term. Pending applications are suspended until the term ends.
+Committee compensation and expense reimbursement under ZIP 1015 are not
+affected.
+
+A grant approved in breach of this ZIP must not be paid. FPF reports breaches
+publicly, and a member who knowingly breaches the rule is expected to leave
+the Committee.
+
+This ZIP has limited privacy implications. Members publish the organizations
+they are associated with, but the names of their family members are not
+published.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 1015 gives the five-seat ZCG Committee final authority over grants paid
+from the 8% ZCG funding stream [^zip-1015-zcg]. The only conflict-of-interest
+rule it sets for Members is that they recuse themselves when voting on
+proposals where they have a financial interest, under the conflict-of-interest
+policy of the FPF Board. Nothing in ZIP 1015 or ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016] stops a Member, or
+an organization they run, from applying for a grant from the same Committee.
+
+Recusal does not remove the conflict in a body this small. A Member who
+recuses still sits with the other four Members on every other decision, often
+over the same months in which their own application is under review. The other
+Members have to judge a colleague's request knowing that the colleague will
+later vote on theirs, or on grants that matter to them. Even when every Member
+acts in good faith, coinholders and applicants cannot tell from the outside
+that a decision was made on the merits. A grant to a sitting Member looks like
+a grant to an insider, and that cost falls on the whole program.
+
+A clear bar is easier to apply than case-by-case recusal. It tells candidates
+in advance what they give up by joining the Committee, it needs no judgment
+call about whether an interest is large enough, and it can be checked from
+public records.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+This ZIP does not create any new disclosure duty for applicants. It does ask
+each Member to publish the organizations they are associated with, and to tell
+FPF confidentially when an immediate family member intends to apply. Members
+already have to recuse when they have a financial interest, so they already
+need to know and declare most of this.
+
+The ZIP does not require the names of a Member's family members to be
+published. Where a family relationship is the reason for a reported
+breach, the public record identifies the Application and the Member but not
+the family member. Readers may still be able to infer the relationship.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* A sitting Member cannot obtain a ZCG Grant for themselves, for an
+  organization they are associated with, or for their immediate family.
+* A Member cannot get around the rule by being named on someone else's grant.
+* The rule is simple to check, and does not depend on a judgment about how
+  large a conflict is.
+* People who already hold grants are not forced to choose between their
+  existing work and serving on the Committee, but cannot grow that work while
+  they serve.
+* Ordinary Committee compensation and expense reimbursement keep working.
+* A grant made in breach of the rule is not paid.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not set a cooling-off period after a Member's Term ends. (See
+  [Open questions](#open-questions).)
+* This ZIP does not change who selects the ZCG Committee, the length of a
+  Term, or the limits on associations with BP/ECC, ZF, and FPF in ZIP 1015.
+* This ZIP does not apply to grants from the Coinholder-Controlled Fund, which
+  are decided by coinholder-amount voting rounds rather than by the ZCG
+  Committee.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Bar on Applications during a Term
+
+During a Member's Term:
+
+1. an Associated Applicant of that Member MUST NOT submit an Application;
+2. the ZCG Committee MUST NOT approve, and FPF MUST NOT pay, a ZCG Grant to an
+   Associated Applicant of that Member, except as permitted in
+   [Grants held before a Term begins](#grants-held-before-a-term-begins); and
+3. the Member MUST NOT be named in any Application, or be paid from any ZCG
+   Grant, as a team member, contractor, subcontractor, advisor, or in any other
+   paid role.
+
+The bar applies whoever the applicant is and however the Application is made,
+including through an intermediary, a fiscal sponsor, or an Autonomous Entity
+operating under FPF.
+
+## Grants held before a Term begins
+
+A ZCG Grant approved before a Member's Term began, to that Member or to one of
+their Associated Applicants, MAY continue to be paid on its existing terms
+during the Term. During the Term:
+
+* the grant MUST NOT be extended, renewed, increased, or given new milestones
+  or scope;
+* the Member MUST recuse from every decision about that grant, including
+  milestone approvals and reviews of whether funding should continue; and
+* the Member MUST disclose the grant on the Zcash Community Forum within 14
+  days after their Term begins.
+
+A grant of indefinite duration that comes up for periodic review during the
+Term, as described in item 2 of the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of
+ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015-zcg], MAY be continued at its existing level, but MUST NOT
+be increased.
+
+## Pending Applications
+
+An Application from an Associated Applicant that is pending when a Member's
+Term begins MUST be suspended, and MUST NOT be decided during the Term. The
+applicant MAY withdraw it, or MAY ask for it to be considered after the Term
+ends.
+
+## Permitted payments to Members
+
+This ZIP does not restrict:
+
+* compensation paid to a Member for their work on the Committee under item 9
+  of the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015-zcg];
+  or
+* reimbursement of a Member's reasonable travel expenses under item 8 of that
+  section.
+
+These payments MUST be approved and reported in the same way as other
+payments from the Discretionary Budget.
+
+## Disclosure by Members
+
+Each Member MUST publish on the Zcash Community Forum, within 14 days after
+their Term begins and again within 14 days after any change, a list of the
+organizations that are their Associated Applicants under item 2 of the
+definition. A Member MUST tell FPF, confidentially, when an immediate family
+member or an organization associated with one intends to apply, so that the
+Application can be refused before it is reviewed.
+
+## Breaches
+
+If an Application is found to breach this ZIP:
+
+* the ZCG Committee MUST refuse it, or, if it has already been approved, MUST
+  revoke the approval;
+* FPF MUST NOT make any further payment on it; and
+* FPF MUST report the breach in its next transparency report under ZIP 1015
+  [^zip-1015-transparency], stating which Application was affected and which
+  Member it related to, without naming any immediate family member.
+
+A Member who knowingly breaches this ZIP, or who knowingly fails to disclose
+an Associated Applicant, SHOULD resign from the Committee. FPF SHOULD seek to
+recover any payment made as a result of a knowing breach.
+
+## Changes to ZIP 1015
+
+In the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015-zcg],
+the following paragraph is added at the end of item 7:
+
+> ZCG Committee members, the organizations they are associated with, and
+> their immediate family members MUST NOT apply for or receive Zcash
+> Community Grants during the member's term, except as provided in ZIP
+> [this ZIP].
+
+## Changes to ZIP 1016
+
+In the section "Zcash Community Grants" of ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016], the
+following sentence is added after the first paragraph, which makes the ZCG
+funding stream subject to the rules in ZIP 1015:
+
+> The restrictions on grants to ZCG Committee members in ZIP [this ZIP] also
+> apply.
+
+## Effective date
+
+This ZIP takes effect on the date its Status becomes Active. It applies to
+Applications submitted on or after that date, and to decisions made on or
+after that date about earlier Applications and grants.
+
+FPF SHOULD include the bar in its agreements with Members and in the terms of
+ZCG Grants, so that it is enforceable under those agreements as well as under
+this ZIP.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Why a bar rather than recusal
+
+The Committee has five seats, so one recusal removes a fifth of the
+decision-makers, and the remaining four have a working relationship with the
+applicant. Recusal handles a Member's interest in a single vote. It does not
+handle the effect that an insider's application has on everyone else at the
+table. A bar is also easier to explain to applicants and coinholders.
+
+## Why organizations and family are included
+
+A bar that covered only the Member personally could be avoided by applying
+through a company the Member runs or partly owns, or through a relative.
+ZIP 1015 already uses financial interest, officer and director roles,
+full-time employment, and immediate family to define "Association"
+[^zip-1015-zcg], so this ZIP reuses that definition rather than inventing a
+new one.
+
+## Why existing grants may continue
+
+Many people suited to the Committee are active builders who may already hold
+a grant. Forcing them to drop that work would shrink the pool of candidates
+and could harm users who rely on it. Letting the grant run on its existing
+terms, while freezing its size and requiring recusal, keeps the work going
+without letting a Member's position help it grow.
+
+## Why only the ZCG Committee
+
+The ZCG Committee decides its own grants. Coinholder-Controlled Fund grants
+are decided by coinholder-amount voting rounds, where Members have no special
+role. Applying this bar to the Coinholder-Controlled Fund would be a separate
+question, and is left open.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* Should the bar continue for a period after the Term ends, for example six
+  or twelve months, to stop a Member arranging a grant to take effect after
+  they leave?
+* Is the organization test too wide? A Member who works full-time at a large
+  organization would bar that whole organization from ZCG Grants. An
+  alternative is to bar only organizations where the Member is an officer,
+  director, or owner of more than a set share.
+* Should a Member's Associated Applicants also be barred from grants from the
+  Coinholder-Controlled Fund?
+* Should a knowing breach remove the Member automatically, rather than only
+  asking them to resign? ZIP 1015 has no removal procedure today.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14, "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^zip-1015]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding](zip-1015.rst)
+
+[^zip-1015-zcg]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding, Zcash Community Grants](zip-1015.rst#zcash-community-grants-zcg)
+
+[^zip-1015-transparency]: [ZIP 1015: Block Subsidy Allocation for Non-Direct Development Funding, Transparency and Accountability](zip-1015.rst#transparency-and-accountability)
+
+[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](zip-1016.md)
