prs.title: Draft ZIP: Establish the ZCG Treasury Committee
prs.author: emersonian
prs.bodyExcerpt: ZCG grant decisions and treasury decisions are currently combined. This draft separates them and requires a published ten-year budget, treasury policy, and hedging strategy to steward the community's funding long-term. Discussion: https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-establish-the-zcg-treasury-com

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,648 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: ZCG Treasury Committee, Budget, and Hedging Plan
+    Owners: Blake Benthall (emersonian) <e@emersonbenthall.com>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-08
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-establish-the-zcg-treasury-committee/59048>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1453>
+    Updates: 1015
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHALL", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document
+are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they
+appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Zcash Community Grants" (or "ZCG"), "ZCG Committee", "Financial
+Privacy Foundation" (or "FPF"), "Autonomous Entities", "Zcash Community
+Advisory Panel" (or "ZCAP"), and "Discretionary Budget" in this document are to
+be interpreted as defined or used in ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015]. In this ZIP the ZCG
+Committee is also called the grants committee, to distinguish it from the
+Treasury Committee.
+
+The terms "Coinholder-Controlled Fund" and "Key-Holder Organizations" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016].
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" in this document are to be interpreted as
+defined in the Zcash protocol specification [^protocol-networks].
+
+"ZEC" refers to the native currency of Zcash on Mainnet.
+
+The terms below are to be interpreted as follows:
+
+ZCG Funding Stream
+
+: Any funding stream whose recipient is FPF, or a successor administrator, for
+  the use of Zcash Community Grants. At the time of writing these are
+  `FS_FPF_ZCG` [^zip-1015-funding-streams] and `FS_FPF_ZCG_H3` [^zip-0214]
+  [^zip-1016-zcg]. The term includes any later funding stream defined for the
+  same purpose, under any name.
+
+Accrued ZCG Funds
+
+: All of the following:
+
+  1. each amount paid to a recipient address of a ZCG Funding Stream, from the
+     block in which the payment is mined;
+  2. each amount donated or otherwise contributed to FPF, or a successor
+     administrator, for the use of Zcash Community Grants, from the time it is
+     received;
+  3. each amount returned to the ZCG program, such as an unspent grant
+     tranche, a recovered grant payment, or an unspent part of the
+     Discretionary Budget; and
+  4. all assets that any of the above is converted into or earns, including
+     fiat currency, stablecoins, other digital assets, deposits, interest,
+     yield, and the proceeds of any hedging position.
+
+  Funds remain Accrued ZCG Funds for as long as they are held, in whatever
+  account, wallet, custodian, or asset they are held. They cease to be Accrued
+  ZCG Funds only when paid out for a grant or an administration expense under
+  the Reference Text.
+
+Reference Text
+
+: The section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)" of ZIP 1015 [^zip-1015-zcg], as
+  amended from time to time.
+
+Accrual Rate
+
+: The share of the block subsidy, or of any other issuance defined by the
+  consensus rules, that is paid to ZCG Funding Streams, together with the start
+  and end heights of those streams.
+
+Treasury Committee
+
+: The ZCG Treasury Committee established under
+  [ZCG Treasury Committee](#zcg-treasury-committee).
+
+Treasury Decision
+
+: A decision of a kind listed in
+  [Treasury Decisions](#treasury-decisions).
+
+Grant Decision
+
+: A decision of a kind listed in [Grant Decisions](#grant-decisions).
+
+Program Budget
+
+: The budget for the ZCG program set by the Treasury Committee under
+  [Program Budget](#program-budget).
+
+Treasury Plan
+
+: The ten-year budget, treasury policy, and hedging strategy described in
+  [Treasury Plan](#treasury-plan).
+
+Activation Date
+
+: The date on which this ZIP becomes Active under ZIP 0 [^zip-0000].
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP changes how Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) manages its funds.
+
+ZCG is required to form a separate Treasury Committee of at least three people.
+Only the Treasury Committee may buy, sell, or convert ZEC, hedge, or set
+budgets. The ZCG grants committee makes grant decisions only, and no person may
+sit on both committees. ZCAP selects every member for a one-year term, sets
+their pay, and can remove a member by a two-thirds vote. Until the Treasury
+Committee is formed, the grants committee may not decide to buy or sell ZEC.
+
+The Treasury Committee must publish a ten-year budget, a treasury plan, and a
+strategy for hedging the risk of a fall in the price of ZEC by 31 March 2027,
+and update them every year.
+
+This ZIP does not decide whether funds already held by ZCG can be taken by a
+later ZIP.
+
+The ZIP has privacy implications for the disclosure of treasury addresses,
+trades, and the personal holdings of committee members, which are discussed
+below.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZCG's balance is held largely in ZEC, while many grant obligations are
+understood by grantees in US dollar terms. The ZCG Funding Stream is scheduled
+to end at the third halving (Mainnet height 6132390 under ZIP 214 Revision 3
+[^zip-0214], expected in late 2028), and could end sooner. A fall in the price
+of ZEC can therefore reduce ZCG's ability to fund work by a large fraction
+within months, with no change to any ZIP.
+
+At the time of writing, the ZCG Committee both chooses grants and decides, with
+FPF, how ZCG's funds are held and when ZEC is sold. These are different skills,
+and combining them creates conflicts: a committee under pressure to fund a
+popular grant may sell ZEC at a poor time, and a committee that decides when
+ZCG sells ZEC has information that could be misused. ZCG also does not publish
+a multi-year budget, a treasury policy, or a hedging policy.
+
+ZCG holds funds that grantees and the community rely on over many years, and
+it has a matching duty to manage them well over that period. A separate committee
+with its own members, a published plan, and clear limits on what each committee may decide is intended
+to meet that duty.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+Publishing treasury addresses, viewing keys, or detailed trade records lets
+anyone link ZCG's holdings and movements over time. This is intended, since the
+community needs to verify how Accrued ZCG Funds are managed, but it can
+also reveal ZCG's counterparties, the timing of its trades, and, through grant
+payments, information about grantees. Publishing planned trades before they are
+executed could also allow others to trade against ZCG.
+
+Holding ZEC in shielded pools improves the privacy of ZCG and its grantees but
+makes public verification depend on ZCG choosing to publish viewing keys or
+attestations.
+
+Disclosure of the personal ZEC holdings of Treasury Committee members, which
+this ZIP requires in order to manage conflicts of interest, reveals sensitive
+financial information about individuals.
+
+The Specification addresses these trade-offs by allowing details of a trade to
+be withheld until it has been executed, and by limiting personal disclosures
+to what is needed to identify conflicts.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* Decisions about how ZCG's funds are held, converted, and hedged, and how much
+  ZCG may spend, are made by a body separate from the body that chooses grants,
+  with no overlapping members.
+* While that separate body is being formed, the grants committee does not
+  decide to buy or sell ZEC.
+* A ten-year budget, treasury plan, and ZEC-depreciation hedging strategy are
+  published by 31 March 2027 and kept current.
+* Converting or hedging Accrued ZCG Funds is possible without being treated as
+  a transfer out of the restricted fund.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not set or change the rate at which funds accrue to ZCG.
+* This ZIP does not decide whether funds already accrued to ZCG may be taken by
+  a later ZIP, network upgrade, or vote.
+* This ZIP does not change how the ZCG Committee is selected, or FPF's ability
+  to veto a decision that would violate Cayman Islands law under point 6 of the
+  Reference Text.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Adoption
+
+This ZIP takes effect on the Activation Date.
+
+## Treasury management
+
+Converting Accrued ZCG Funds from one asset to another, moving them between
+accounts, wallets, or custodians controlled by the ZCG program's administrator,
+and opening or closing hedging positions, do not take funds out of ZCG's
+restricted fund, provided that:
+
+* the resulting assets remain Accrued ZCG Funds and are accounted for in ZCG's
+  restricted fund;
+* the action is a Treasury Decision made by the Treasury Committee, or is
+  permitted by
+  [Interim restriction on the grants committee](#interim-restriction-on-the-grants-committee);
+* after the first Treasury Plan is published, the action is consistent with the
+  Treasury Plan then in effect; and
+* the action is reported in ZCG's next quarterly report.
+
+Reasonable transaction, custody, and hedging costs are administration expenses
+under the Reference Text. A loss caused by a fall in the price of an asset, or
+by closing a hedge at a loss, is not a misuse of Accrued ZCG Funds if the
+action that led to it complied with this section.
+
+## ZCG Treasury Committee
+
+### Formation
+
+ZCG SHALL establish a ZCG Treasury Committee no later than 45 days after the
+Activation Date.
+
+ZCAP, or any successor process that selects members of the ZCG Committee, MUST
+select all members of the Treasury Committee, including its initial members,
+using the same voting process it uses to select members of the ZCG Committee.
+The ZCG Committee and FPF MUST NOT appoint Treasury Committee members.
+
+The initial members SHALL adopt the Treasury Committee's charter, and publish
+it on the Zcash Community Forum, within 30 days after they are selected.
+
+### Membership
+
+The Treasury Committee MUST have at least three members.
+
+No person SHALL be a member of both the ZCG Committee and the Treasury
+Committee at the same time.
+
+No person who is a member of the ZCG Committee on the Activation Date SHALL be
+appointed to the Treasury Committee, even if they later leave the ZCG
+Committee. Former members who left the ZCG Committee before the Activation
+Date are eligible.
+
+The restrictions on association with BP/ECC, ZF, and FPF in point 7 of the
+Reference Text apply to the Treasury Committee in the same way as to the ZCG
+Committee. A majority of Treasury Committee members MUST NOT have an
+association, as defined in that point, with FPF.
+
+Members SHOULD have relevant experience, such as in treasury management,
+finance, risk management, or digital asset custody.
+
+### Terms
+
+Each member serves a term of one year, as for members of the ZCG Committee
+under point 7 of the Reference Text. A member MAY be selected again for further
+terms.
+
+So that seats come up for selection at different times, ZCAP MAY give some of
+the initial members a first term of six months. Every later term is one year.
+
+A member MAY resign at any time by notice posted on the Zcash Community Forum.
+
+A vacancy, however it arises, SHALL be filled by ZCAP for the rest of the
+term, within 45 days after it arises.
+
+### Charter
+
+The charter MUST specify:
+
+* quorum and voting rules;
+* a personal trading policy meeting the requirements of
+  [Conflicts of interest and personal trading](#conflicts-of-interest-and-personal-trading);
+  and
+* how the charter may be amended.
+
+The charter MUST NOT conflict with this ZIP, and MUST NOT give the ZCG
+Committee any power to remove Treasury Committee members, to direct Treasury
+Decisions, or to amend the charter.
+
+### Compensation
+
+Treasury Committee members SHALL be paid for their work, at a rate set by ZCAP
+or its successor process in the same way as compensation of ZCG Committee
+members under point 9 of the Reference Text. Compensation is an administration
+expense, and the rate SHALL be published.
+
+### Removal
+
+A Treasury Committee member MAY be removed before the end of their term only
+by the process in this section.
+
+Grounds. A member may be removed for:
+
+* a material breach of this ZIP or the charter, including the disclosure and
+  personal trading rules;
+* acting outside the authority given by this ZIP;
+* fraud, dishonesty, or a criminal conviction related to their role;
+* missing three consecutive meetings, or more than half of the meetings in any
+  six-month period, without good reason; or
+* being unable to carry out their duties.
+
+Motion. Any member of ZCAP, the ZCG Committee, or the Treasury Committee, or
+FPF, MAY file a motion to remove a member. The motion MUST be posted on the
+Zcash Community Forum, and MUST state the grounds and the facts relied on.
+
+Response. The member named in the motion MUST be given at least 14 days after
+the motion is posted to respond publicly before any vote opens.
+
+Vote. ZCAP SHALL then vote on the motion, using the same voting process it
+uses to select members of the ZCG Committee, over a period of at least seven
+days. The member is removed if at least two-thirds of the votes cast are in
+favor, and at least half of ZCAP's members vote. ZCAP SHALL publish the
+result and the number of votes for and against.
+
+Suspension. Where a motion alleges a breach of the personal trading rules, or
+misuse of funds, a majority of the other Treasury Committee members MAY
+suspend the member from all Treasury Decisions until the vote ends, and MUST
+publish that they have done so.
+
+Effect. A removed member leaves office when the result is published. They are
+not eligible to be selected to the Treasury Committee or the ZCG Committee
+for three years afterwards. Their seat is filled as a vacancy under
+[Terms](#terms).
+
+### Authority
+
+Treasury Decisions made by the Treasury Committee are final and do not require
+the approval of the ZCG Committee or FPF's board, but are subject to veto if FPF
+determines that they would violate Cayman Islands law or FPF's reporting
+requirements or other obligations, in the same way as ZCG Committee decisions
+under point 6 of the Reference Text. FPF SHALL execute Treasury Decisions that
+are not vetoed, and SHALL publish the reasons for any veto.
+
+The Treasury Committee has no authority to use Accrued ZCG Funds other than as
+the Reference Text permits, or to transfer them out of the ZCG program.
+
+### Conflicts of interest and personal trading
+
+Each Treasury Committee member MUST disclose, on appointment and in each
+quarterly report, whether they hold, or have a financial interest in, ZEC or
+financial instruments whose value depends on the price of ZEC, and the
+approximate size of that holding in ranges set by the charter.
+
+A Treasury Committee member MUST NOT trade ZEC, or instruments whose value
+depends on the price of ZEC, while they know of a Treasury Decision that has not
+yet been fully executed and disclosed, or within a period set by the charter
+before and after such a decision.
+
+A Treasury Committee member MUST recuse themselves from a Treasury Decision in
+which they have a personal financial interest other than their general holding
+of ZEC, such as an interest in a proposed counterparty or custodian.
+
+### Transparency of the Treasury Committee
+
+The Treasury Committee SHALL publish minutes of each meeting within 14 days of
+the meeting. Details of a planned trade or hedge MAY be withheld from the
+minutes until it has been executed, and SHALL be published no later than ZCG's
+next quarterly report after execution.
+
+## Separation of grant and treasury decisions
+
+### Treasury Decisions
+
+The following are Treasury Decisions:
+
+* buying, selling, or converting ZEC or any other asset held as Accrued ZCG
+  Funds, including the amount and timing of any sale or purchase;
+* setting asset allocation and the size of any liquidity reserve;
+* opening, adjusting, or closing a hedging position;
+* selecting custodians, exchanges, banks, and other treasury counterparties,
+  and, together with FPF, setting the custody and signing arrangements for
+  Accrued ZCG Funds;
+* setting the Program Budget; and
+* preparing, adopting, and updating the Treasury Plan.
+
+### Grant Decisions
+
+The following are Grant Decisions:
+
+* approving, rejecting, modifying, renewing, or terminating grants;
+* issuing requests for proposals;
+* setting and assessing grant milestones; and
+* approving disbursements from the Discretionary Budget under point 8 of the
+  Reference Text.
+
+### Rules on separation
+
+The ZCG Committee MUST NOT make Treasury Decisions.
+
+The Treasury Committee MUST NOT make Grant Decisions, and MUST NOT make a
+Treasury Decision for the purpose of favoring or disfavoring a particular grant
+or applicant.
+
+The ZCG Committee MUST NOT approve a grant, or a disbursement from the
+Discretionary Budget, that would cause total commitments in a budget period to
+exceed the amount set for that period in the Program Budget. The ZCG Committee
+MAY ask the Treasury Committee to amend the Program Budget, and SHALL publish any
+such request.
+
+Whether a grant is denominated in ZEC or in another currency is a Grant
+Decision, but the ZCG Committee SHALL follow any policy on grant denomination
+set in the Treasury Plan.
+
+## Interim restriction on the grants committee
+
+From the Activation Date until the Treasury Committee is established, the ZCG
+Committee MUST NOT make any decision to buy, sell, or convert ZEC, and MUST NOT
+set or change any budget.
+
+During that period, FPF MAY convert ZEC only to the extent needed to pay grant
+installments and administration expenses that were approved before or during
+that period and that fall due within the following 30 days. Such conversions
+SHALL be made at or shortly before the time of payment, without discretion as
+to timing, and SHALL be reported in ZCG's next quarterly report.
+
+The ZCG Committee MAY continue to make Grant Decisions during that period.
+
+## Program Budget
+
+The Treasury Committee SHALL set a Program Budget for each calendar year,
+stating the maximum total amount that may be committed in that year for:
+
+* grants; and
+* administration expenses, including the Discretionary Budget.
+
+The Program Budget MUST provide for the Discretionary Budget and committee
+compensation as determined by ZCAP under points 8 and 9 of the Reference Text.
+
+The Treasury Committee SHALL publish the Program Budget, and any amendment to
+it, on the Zcash Community Forum within 7 days of adopting it.
+
+Until the first Program Budget is adopted, no budget limit under this ZIP
+applies to Grant Decisions.
+
+## Treasury Plan
+
+### Deadline
+
+The Treasury Committee SHALL publish the Treasury Plan on the Zcash Community
+Forum and on the ZCG website no later than 31 March 2027. If the Treasury
+Committee is established later than 30 January 2027, the deadline is instead
+60 days after it is established.
+
+The Treasury Committee SHOULD publish a draft of the Treasury Plan for comment
+at least 21 days before publishing the final version, and SHOULD respond
+publicly to substantive comments.
+
+FPF SHALL provide the Treasury Committee with the financial information,
+custody details, and professional support that it reasonably needs to prepare
+the Treasury Plan. The cost of independent financial or legal advice for this
+purpose is an administration expense.
+
+### Ten-year budget
+
+The Treasury Plan MUST include a budget for each calendar year from 2027 to
+2036 inclusive that:
+
+1. states the balance of Accrued ZCG Funds by asset, with its value in ZEC and
+   in US dollars, as of a stated recent date;
+2. projects income under at least the following Accrual Rate scenarios:
+   * the ZCG Funding Stream continues to its scheduled end at Mainnet height
+     6132390 and is not renewed;
+   * the ZCG Funding Stream is renewed after that height at its current
+     percentage of the block subsidy; and
+   * the ZCG Funding Stream ends at the first network upgrade after the
+     Treasury Plan is published;
+3. considers at least three ZEC price scenarios, one of which assumes that the
+   price of ZEC falls by at least 75% from its price at the time the Treasury
+   Plan is prepared and does not recover during the budget period;
+4. sets out planned spending by category, including at least major grants,
+   smaller grants and community programs, requests for proposals, and
+   administration (including the Discretionary Budget, committee compensation,
+   and treasury costs);
+5. shows existing commitments separately from planned new spending;
+6. states the expected runway in each scenario; and
+7. states the minimum spending needed to keep the ZCG program operating, and
+   how long existing Accrued ZCG Funds alone could sustain it.
+
+### Treasury policy
+
+The Treasury Plan MUST include a treasury policy that specifies:
+
+1. target ranges for holdings in ZEC, fiat currency, stablecoins, and other
+   assets, with reasons, and a minimum low-risk liquidity reserve sufficient
+   to pay committed grants for a stated period;
+2. custody and key management arrangements, including signing thresholds and
+   backups, consistent with the "Security precautions" section of ZIP 1016;
+3. whether ZEC is kept in shielded pools, and how the community can verify
+   balances (for example by viewing keys or periodic attestations);
+4. limits on exposure to any single bank, custodian, exchange, stablecoin
+   issuer, or other counterparty;
+5. confirmation that Accrued ZCG Funds will not be lent to related parties,
+   pledged for unrelated obligations, or used for speculative trading, and
+   that leverage will be used, if at all, only within a hedge described in the
+   hedging strategy;
+6. whether grants are denominated in ZEC, in US dollars, or a mix; and
+7. how treasury actions will be reported in ZCG's quarterly reports and
+   dashboard.
+
+### Hedging strategy
+
+The Treasury Plan MUST include a strategy for managing the risk that a fall in
+the price of ZEC leaves ZCG unable to meet its commitments. The strategy MUST:
+
+1. measure ZCG's exposure: the gap between its ZEC holdings and its
+   obligations fixed in other currencies, now and over the budget period;
+2. describe the methods to be used, which MAY include scheduled conversion of
+   income, a low-risk reserve matched to committed grants, denominating some
+   grants in ZEC, put options or collars, or other methods, with each method's
+   expected cost, counterparty and custody risks, legal constraints, and
+   likely effect on the ZEC market;
+3. set limits on the size and type of positions, so that no position increases
+   ZCG's overall exposure to the price of ZEC;
+4. set a schedule or triggers for review and rebalancing; and
+5. explain how it balances reducing risk against keeping ZCG's interests
+   aligned with the success of ZEC.
+
+### Updates and reporting
+
+The Treasury Committee SHALL review the Treasury Plan at least once a year, and
+SHALL publish an updated Treasury Plan, extended so that it covers the next ten
+calendar years, no later than 31 March of each year from 2028.
+
+Each ZCG quarterly report required by ZIP 1015 SHALL include:
+
+* the balance of Accrued ZCG Funds by asset, with its value in ZEC and in US
+  dollars;
+* the treasury actions taken in the quarter and their results; and
+* actual commitments and spending compared with the Program Budget, with an
+  explanation of any material difference.
+
+### Status of the Treasury Plan obligations
+
+The obligations in [Program Budget](#program-budget) and
+[Treasury Plan](#treasury-plan) are added to the obligations that FPF accepts on
+behalf of ZCG under the section "Transparency and Accountability" of ZIP 1015
+[^zip-1015-transparency].
+
+## Enforcement
+
+Any member of the community MAY publicly report a suspected breach of this ZIP.
+FPF or the committee concerned SHALL respond publicly within 30 days.
+
+A breach of this ZIP by FPF is a violation of FPF's obligations under ZIP 1015,
+to which the enforcement provisions of ZIP 1015 apply
+[^zip-1015-enforcement].
+
+## Changes to ZIP 1015
+
+In the section "Zcash Community Grants (ZCG)", after the paragraph beginning
+"FPF SHALL be contractually required to recognize the ZCG slice of the Dev Fund
+as a Restricted Fund donation", insert:
+
+> Treasury management decisions for these funds, including any decision to buy
+> or sell ZEC and the setting of budgets, are made by the ZCG Treasury
+> Committee as specified in ZIP [this ZIP]. The ZCG Committee MUST NOT make
+> such decisions.
+
+In the section "Transparency and Accountability", add to the list of
+obligations:
+
+> * Publication and annual update of a Program Budget and of a ten-year budget,
+>   treasury plan, and ZEC-depreciation hedging strategy, as specified in
+>   ZIP [this ZIP].
+
+## Testnet-specific considerations
+
+This ZIP has no effect on Testnet. Testnet funds are not Accrued ZCG Funds.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Rationale for allowing conversion and hedging
+
+Read literally, a rule that accrued funds may not be moved for any purpose other
+than grants could prevent ZCG from converting ZEC to pay a grant denominated in
+US dollars, or from hedging. The ZIP therefore treats any action that keeps the
+value inside the restricted fund as treasury management, and requires the
+policy governing it to be published.
+
+## Rationale for a separate Treasury Committee
+
+Separating the people who choose grants from the people who decide when to sell
+ZEC reduces the risk that grant pressure drives poorly timed sales, and limits
+the number of people with advance knowledge of ZCG's trades. It is a common
+arrangement in endowments and foundations, where an investment or finance
+committee is distinct from the program committee. ZCAP selects every
+member, including the first ones, so that the grants committee never chooses
+the people who decide when its funds are sold. Members serve one-year terms,
+are paid at a rate ZCAP sets, and can be removed only by a two-thirds ZCAP
+vote after public charges and a chance to respond, as for any other role that
+handles this much money.
+
+The interim restriction prevents the grants committee from making large
+discretionary sales or purchases while the new committee is being formed. The
+narrow exception for conversions needed to pay approved grants is included so
+that grantees are not left unpaid during that period.
+
+## Rationale for the deadline
+
+A deadline of 31 March 2027 allows time to form the Treasury Committee and hold
+a comment period on a draft plan, and puts the first Treasury Plan in place well
+before the scheduled end of the ZCG Funding Stream in late 2028.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* Is 45 days long enough for ZCAP to select the initial members, or should the
+  window be 60 days?
+* Should a community petition, for example by a set number of Forum members,
+  also be able to start a removal motion?
+* Should the size of the Discretionary Budget move from ZCAP to the Treasury
+  Committee, given that the Treasury Committee sets the Program Budget?
+* Is the 30-day exception for conversions needed to pay approved grants during
+  the interim period acceptable, or should all conversions wait for the
+  Treasury Committee?
+* The 31 March 2027 deadline can be met without the 60-day extension only if
+  this ZIP becomes Active by mid-December 2026. Is that realistic?
+
+
+# References
+

+

+

prs.title: Draft ZIP: Minimum Human Participation in Coinholder Votes
prs.author: emersonian
prs.bodyExcerpt: Today’s coin threshold can be met by whoever holds enough coins, and does not ensure that a minimum amount of humans participated in a potentially-binding coinholder vote. This draft requires a minimum number of distinct verified people to take part before a coinholder-amount voting round can approv

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,430 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Update to ZIP 1016: Minimum Human Participation and Published Proof-of-Personhood for Coinholder Votes
+    Owners: Blake Benthall (emersonian) <e@emersonbenthall.com>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-08
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-minimum-human-participation-in-coinholder-votes/59045>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1450>
+    Updates: 1016
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", and "MAY" in this document are to
+be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" in this document are to be interpreted as
+defined in the Zcash protocol specification [^protocol-networks].
+
+The terms "Coinholder-Controlled Fund" and "Key-Holder Organizations" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016], as
+amended by any ZIP that updates the membership of the Key-Holder Organizations
+(see for example [^draft-mcgee-keyholders]).
+
+"ZEC" refers to the native currency of Zcash on Mainnet.
+
+The terms below are to be interpreted as follows:
+
+Coinholder-amount voting round
+
+: Any coinholder vote held under ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016-disbursement], in which
+  each ballot is weighted by the amount of ZEC that the voter proves control of.
+  This includes votes on grant applications, separate votes on competing
+  proposals, and additional votes on whether funding of an existing grant should
+  continue.
+
+Coinholder poll
+
+: A coinholder-amount voting round, or any other poll of ZEC holders that is
+  organized, administered, or certified by one or more Key-Holder Organizations,
+  or that a ZIP cites as evidence of coinholder support or opposition.
+
+Ballot
+
+: A single vote cast in a coinholder poll on a single question. A ballot is one
+  of Approve, Reject, or Abstain (or the equivalent options of a poll that is
+  not a yes/no question).
+
+ZEC voted
+
+: ZEC voted in a coinholder poll, for a given question, is the total amount of
+  ZEC committed by all ballots cast on that question, including ballots that
+  Abstain.
+
+Verified coinholder-person
+
+: A natural person who, for a given coinholder poll, has been verified under the
+  Human Verification Methodology in effect for that poll as (a) being a unique
+  natural person, and (b) controlling at least the Minimum Personhood Balance of
+  ZEC at the snapshot height used for that poll.
+
+Human Verification Methodology
+
+: The document described in [Human Verification
+  Methodology](#human-verification-methodology).
+
+Personhood Attestation
+
+: The Personhood Attestation for a coinholder poll is the report described in
+  [Personhood Attestation](#personhood-attestation).
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP updates ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016] so that a coinholder-amount voting round
+can only approve a grant, or otherwise bind the Key-Holder Organizations, if:
+
+* the ZEC threshold of ZIP 1016 is met, as it stands or as raised by the
+  companion quorum draft [^draft-quorum];
+* ballots were cast on the question by at least 50 distinct verified
+  coinholder-persons; and
+* the Key-Holder Organizations published their Human Verification Methodology
+  in advance, and publish a Personhood Attestation for the result.
+
+It requires the Key-Holder Organizations to publish the methodology they use
+to verify that participants are distinct humans, in a way that preserves the
+privacy of voters and of their vote choices. A coinholder poll that does not
+meet these conditions is advisory only.
+
+This ZIP does not change how ballots are weighted. Coinholder-amount voting
+rounds continue to be decided by the amount of ZEC voted. The human
+participation requirement is a floor on legitimacy, not a second vote.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 1016 requires a minimum amount of ZEC to be voted, with a simple majority
+in favor, for a grant proposal to be approved [^zip-1016-disbursement]. That
+threshold counts coins, never people. As of late 2026, the Grayscale Zcash ETF
+alone held about 594,293 ZEC [^grayscale], more than the whole 420,000 ZEC
+threshold, and Cypherpunk Technologies about 326,417 ZEC [^blockworks-q3].
+A single holder could therefore make a vote valid with no one else taking
+part. The author does not claim that anyone has done so. The concern is that a
+result alone cannot show that coinholders in general, rather than one balance
+sheet, supported a grant.
+
+The companion quorum draft [^draft-quorum] raises the threshold to 1,000,000
+ZEC, but any coin threshold can be met by whoever accumulates enough coins.
+This ZIP therefore also requires a minimum number of distinct humans to have
+taken part.
+
+Counting humans requires a method for verifying personhood. Today no ZIP
+defines "coinholder" [^zip-1016], and the voting model that ZIP 1016 says will
+be "specified in another ZIP [TBD]" [^zip-1016-ccf] has not been written. The
+Key-Holder Organizations already organize and certify votes, and so act as de
+facto election administrators. If they are to count humans, the community
+needs to be able to see and critique how they do it, before the vote rather
+than after.
+
+Zcash's purpose is financial privacy. Any proof-of-personhood process for
+Zcash coinholder polls must therefore be designed so that verifying that a
+voter is a unique human does not reveal who that voter is, which shielded
+addresses they control, or how they voted.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+Counting distinct humans means that someone has to check personhood, and any
+such check can leak information. A careless process could link a voter's
+legal identity to their shielded holdings, reveal which addresses or notes
+they control, or record how they voted. Any of these would undermine the
+financial privacy that Zcash exists to provide, and could expose voters to
+coercion or targeting.
+
+This ZIP does not choose a proof-of-personhood technology. Instead, the
+Specification limits what a Human Verification Methodology may require and
+what may be published. Participants do not have to publish their legal
+identity, move funds out of a shielded pool, or reveal a shielded address or
+viewing key, and no link between a person and their ballot is recorded. The
+Personhood Attestation reports counts only. The methodology also has to say
+what data is collected, who sees it, and how long it is kept, so that the
+community can judge the remaining privacy risk before each vote.
+
+Taking part in personhood verification is optional. A coinholder who does not
+want to be verified can still vote, and their ZEC is counted as before.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* A coinholder-amount voting round cannot bind the Key-Holder Organizations
+  unless a minimum number of distinct humans participated.
+* The method by which humans are counted is published before voting begins,
+  and cannot be changed during a voting window.
+* The process does not require publication of any voter's identity, the
+  addresses they control, or the link between a person and their ballot.
+* The outcome of every coinholder poll states whether it met the conditions
+  to be binding, so that the community can tell a binding result from an
+  advisory one.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not introduce person-weighted (one-person-one-vote) decision
+  making, and does not change the weighting of ballots by ZEC amount.
+* This ZIP does not specify a particular proof-of-personhood technology.
+  Choosing one is left to the Key-Holder Organizations, subject to the
+  publication, privacy, and audit requirements below.
+* This ZIP does not change the ZEC threshold of ZIP 1016. That is the
+  subject of the companion quorum draft [^draft-quorum].
+* This ZIP does not change the veto process of ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016-veto], the
+  funding streams, or the membership of the Key-Holder Organizations.
+* This ZIP does not specify the general voting model that ZIP 1016 defers to
+  "another ZIP [TBD]", although it constrains any such model.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Changes to ZIP 1016
+
+In the "Disbursement process" section of ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016-disbursement],
+the following sentence is added after the sentence that sets the minimum
+amount of ZEC to be voted:
+
+> In addition, ballots on a grant proposal MUST have been cast by at least 50
+> distinct verified coinholder-persons, and the other conditions in ZIP [this
+> ZIP] MUST be met, for the grant proposal to be approved.
+
+In the "Testnet-specific considerations" section of ZIP 1016, the following
+sentence is added after the sentence about the Mainnet ZEC threshold: "The
+minimum number of verified coinholder-persons applied to Mainnet coinholder
+votes does not apply to these rehearsals, but Testnet rehearsals SHOULD
+exercise the Human Verification Methodology."
+
+## Minimum human participation
+
+A question in a coinholder-amount voting round MUST NOT be treated as approved
+unless ballots on that question were cast by at least 50 distinct verified
+coinholder-persons. Ballots that Abstain count toward this minimum.
+
+Each verified coinholder-person counts at most once toward this minimum for a
+given question, regardless of how many addresses, wallets, or ballots they
+use.
+
+A verified coinholder-person counts toward this minimum regardless of how much
+ZEC they hold above the Minimum Personhood Balance, and regardless of which
+way they voted.
+
+Coinholders who do not take part in personhood verification MAY still vote.
+Their ZEC counts toward ZEC voted and toward the majority as before. They do
+not count toward the minimum number of verified coinholder-persons.
+
+## Human Verification Methodology
+
+The Key-Holder Organizations MUST jointly publish a Human Verification
+Methodology, and MUST publish it on the Zcash Community Forum and at a stable
+URL linked from the announcement of each coinholder poll.
+
+The Human Verification Methodology for a coinholder poll MUST be published at
+least 30 days before the voting window for that poll opens, matching the
+existing 30-day community review period for grant applications
+[^zip-1016-disbursement]. It MUST NOT be changed between that publication and
+the publication of the Personhood Attestation for that poll, except to
+correct a security vulnerability, in which case the change and the reason for
+it MUST be published immediately.
+
+The Human Verification Methodology MUST describe at least:
+
+1. Verification method: how a participant demonstrates that they are a
+   unique natural person, including any third-party services, credentials,
+   in-person events, social attestation, or cryptographic protocols used.
+2. Uniqueness: how the process prevents one person from being counted
+   more than once for the same question (Sybil resistance), and the known
+   limits of that protection.
+3. Coinholder link: how a verified person is linked to control of at
+   least the Minimum Personhood Balance of ZEC at the poll's snapshot height,
+   without revealing which addresses or notes they control.
+4. Minimum Personhood Balance: the minimum amount of ZEC that a person
+   must control to be counted as a verified coinholder-person. This MUST be
+   greater than zero, and SHOULD be no more than 1 ZEC.
+5. Privacy: what data is collected about participants, who can see it,
+   how the link between a person and their ballot is kept from being
+   recorded or disclosed, and how long any data is retained.
+6. Accessibility: how a coinholder can take part regardless of
+   jurisdiction, wallet software, or whether they hold ZEC in shielded or
+   transparent addresses, and what alternatives exist for those who cannot
+   use the primary method.
+7. Administration: which Key-Holder Organization or contracted third
+   party operates each part of the process, and any conflicts of interest
+   they have in the poll's outcome.
+8. Audit: how an independent party, or the public, can check the count of
+   verified coinholder-persons without learning their identities.
+9. Disputes: how a participant, applicant, or member of the community can
+   challenge a verification decision or the published count, and who decides.
+
+The Human Verification Methodology:
+
+* MUST NOT require that a participant's legal identity be published, or be
+  disclosed to any party other than one named in the methodology under item 7.
+* MUST NOT record or publish any link between a verified coinholder-person and
+  the content of their ballot.
+* MUST NOT require that a participant move funds out of a shielded pool, or
+  reveal a shielded address or viewing key to any party.
+* SHOULD prefer methods in which no single party learns both a participant's
+  identity and the fact that they took part in the poll.
+* SHOULD be the same for every question in a voting window.
+
+Any Key-Holder Organization MAY additionally publish its own objections to, or
+reservations about, a jointly published methodology.
+
+## Personhood Attestation
+
+Within 7 days after a voting window closes, and before any disbursement is
+signed on the basis of a vote held in that window, the Key-Holder
+Organizations MUST publish a Personhood Attestation that states, for each
+question:
+
+* the ZEC voted, the ZEC in favor, the ZEC against, and the ZEC abstaining
+  (ZEC voted includes abstaining ZEC);
+* the number of distinct verified coinholder-persons who cast a ballot on it;
+* whether each of the conditions in this ZIP was met; and
+* a reference to the Human Verification Methodology that was in effect.
+
+The Personhood Attestation MUST be signed by each Key-Holder Organization
+that agrees with it. A Key-Holder Organization that does not agree with the
+attestation MUST publish its reasons.
+
+The Personhood Attestation MUST NOT contain any information that identifies a
+verified coinholder-person or links them to their ballot.
+
+## Binding and advisory results
+
+A coinholder poll is "binding" only if:
+
+1. a Human Verification Methodology was published for it as required above;
+2. the minimum amount of ZEC required by ZIP 1016, as amended at the time
+   the voting window opens, was voted on the question;
+3. ballots on the question were cast by at least 50 distinct verified
+   coinholder-persons; and
+4. a Personhood Attestation for it has been published, and is signed by at
+   least two Key-Holder Organizations.
+
+A coinholder poll that is not binding is "advisory". In particular:
+
+* The Key-Holder Organizations MUST NOT sign a disbursement from the
+  Coinholder-Controlled Fund on the basis of a coinholder-amount voting round
+  that is not binding. A grant proposal on which the vote is advisory is not
+  approved, whatever the outcome of the ballots.
+* Where a vote on whether funding of an existing grant should continue is
+  advisory, the existing grant continues on its existing terms, as if the
+  vote had not been held.
+* A ZIP or Key-Holder Organization communication MUST NOT describe the result
+  of an advisory coinholder poll as a decision, approval, or mandate of
+  coinholders. It MAY report the result, labeled as advisory, with the
+  Personhood Attestation.
+
+The Key-Holder Organizations' veto rights under ZIP 1016
+[^zip-1016-veto] are unchanged and apply only to binding votes.
+
+## Scope
+
+This ZIP applies to every coinholder-amount voting round under ZIP 1016
+[^zip-1016], including separate votes on competing proposals and votes on the
+continuation of an existing grant.
+
+For a coinholder poll that is not a coinholder-amount voting round, such as a
+sentiment poll on a protocol change, this ZIP does not decide what weight the
+community gives the result. The poll's organizers SHOULD apply the Human
+Verification Methodology, and the result MUST be reported as binding or
+advisory under the rules above.
+
+## Activation
+
+This ZIP takes effect for any coinholder poll whose voting window opens on or
+after the later of:
+
+* the date this ZIP's Status becomes Active; and
+* 30 days after the first Human Verification Methodology is published.
+
+Until then, coinholder-amount voting rounds continue under the existing rules
+of ZIP 1016.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Why a human minimum rather than human-weighted votes
+
+Changing to one-person-one-vote would be a larger change to ZIP 1016's
+funding model, which was adopted on the basis of giving coinholders a voice
+in proportion to their holdings. A minimum number of distinct participants
+keeps coin-weighted decisions, but requires evidence that a grant was
+approved by more than a handful of parties. It is a quorum of people, not a
+vote of people.
+
+Parallel person-based polls, such as the coinperson poll planned for
+December 2026 [^coinperson], can inform whether a stronger, bicameral
+requirement is warranted in a future ZIP.
+
+## Why 50 humans
+
+50 is low enough that any genuinely community-supported proposal should be
+able to reach it, and high enough that a single holder, or a small group of
+insiders, cannot reach it without visibly recruiting others. The number of
+distinct participants in past rounds has not been published, so the
+threshold can be revisited once Personhood Attestations provide data.
+
+## Why the Key-Holder Organizations publish the methodology
+
+The Key-Holder Organizations already agree the grant application process,
+decide which proposals are in competition, and sign disbursements
+[^zip-1016-disbursement]. They are the parties who would act on a
+personhood count, and are the natural parties to be accountable for it.
+Requiring publication before the voting window opens means that the method
+can be reviewed alongside the grant applications, and cannot be adjusted
+after the fact to change an outcome.
+
+The ZIP sets requirements on what the methodology must disclose and protect,
+rather than choosing a technology, because proof-of-personhood methods are
+changing quickly and each has different privacy and accessibility trade-offs.
+
+## Why privacy constraints
+
+A proof-of-personhood process that links identities to shielded holdings or
+to ballots would undermine the financial privacy that Zcash exists to
+provide, and could expose voters to coercion. The constraints in this ZIP are
+intended to make the count of humans checkable without making any individual
+human visible.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* Should this ZIP stay separate from the quorum draft [^draft-quorum], or be
+  merged with it after community polling?
+* Should the human minimum scale with the size of the grant, for example
+  requiring more verified coinholder-persons for grants above a given amount?
+* Should the Minimum Personhood Balance be fixed in this ZIP rather than set
+  by the methodology?
+* Should the Personhood Attestation require all of the Key-Holder
+  Organizations, rather than two?
+* Should Zcash Community Grants, or another party independent of the
+  Key-Holder Organizations, audit the Personhood Attestation?
+* ZIP 1016 only recommends that the Key-Holder Organizations sign the
+  transactions for an approved grant. Should signing be made mandatory for
+  binding votes?
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14, "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol-networks]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 3.12: Mainnet and Testnet](protocol/protocol.pdf#networks)
+
+[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](zip-1016.md)
+
+[^zip-1016-ccf]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model, Coinholder-Controlled Fund](zip-1016.md#coinholder-controlled-fund)
+
+[^zip-1016-disbursement]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model, Disbursement process](zip-1016.md#disbursement-process)
+
+[^zip-1016-veto]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model, Veto process](zip-1016.md#veto-process)
+
+[^draft-quorum]: Draft ZIP: Update to ZIP 1016: Raise the Coinholder Vote Threshold to 1,000,000 ZEC (separate draft)
+
+[^draft-mcgee-keyholders]: [Draft ZIP: Update to ZIP 1016 & ZIP 271: Key-Holder Organizations](draft-mcgee-keyholders-organizations.md)
+
+[^grayscale]: [Grayscale Zcash ETF (ZCSH) holdings, as of 2026-10-30](https://www.thezcashetf.com/)
+
+[^blockworks-q3]: [Blockworks, Zcash Token Holder Report, Q3 2026](https://app.blockworks.com/report/zcash-token-holder-report-q3-2026)
+
+[^coinperson]: [coinperson.org](https://coinperson.org/)

prs.title: Draft ZIP: Raise the Coinholder Vote Threshold to 1,000,000 ZEC
prs.author: emersonian
prs.bodyExcerpt: Single known ZEC holders can currently satisfy the 420,000 ZEC threshold in ZIP 1016. This draft raises it to a level aligned with recent coinholder-amount polling participation, and clarifies how abstentions are counted. Discussion: https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-raise-the-coinholder-vote-t

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,236 @@
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Update to ZIP 1016: Raise the Coinholder Vote Threshold to 1,000,000 ZEC
+    Owners: Blake Benthall (emersonian) <e@emersonbenthall.com>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Process
+    Created: 2026-11-08
+    License: MIT
+    Discussions-To: <https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/zip-raise-the-coinholder-vote-threshold/59044>
+    Pull-Request: <https://github.com/zcash/zips/pull/1449>
+    Updates: 1016
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST" and "SHOULD" in this document are to be interpreted as
+described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.
+
+The terms "Mainnet" and "Testnet" in this document are to be interpreted as
+defined in the Zcash protocol specification [^protocol-networks].
+
+The terms "Coinholder-Controlled Fund" and "Key-Holder Organizations" in this
+document are to be interpreted as described in ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016], as
+amended by any ZIP that updates the membership of the Key-Holder Organizations
+(see for example [^draft-mcgee-keyholders]).
+
+"ZEC" refers to the native currency of Zcash on Mainnet.
+
+The terms below are to be interpreted as follows:
+
+Coinholder-amount voting round
+
+: Any coinholder vote held under ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016-disbursement], in which
+  each ballot is weighted by the amount of ZEC that the voter proves control of.
+  This includes votes on grant applications, separate votes on competing
+  proposals, and additional votes on whether funding of an existing grant should
+  continue.
+
+ZEC voted
+
+: For a given question in a coinholder-amount voting round, the total amount of
+  ZEC committed by all ballots cast on that question, including ballots that
+  abstain.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP raises the minimum amount of ZEC that must be voted for a
+coinholder-amount voting round under ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016] to approve a grant,
+from 420,000 ZEC to 1,000,000 ZEC. At current holdings, this means that no
+single publicly known holder of ZEC, and not even the two largest known
+holders together, can make a vote valid on their own. The top proposal in the
+most recent round drew about 2.18 million ZEC, worth about US$3.1 billion, so
+the new threshold is still well within reach of proposals with broad
+support.
+
+It also writes down how abstentions are counted, which ZIP 1016 never stated:
+abstaining ZEC counts toward the 1,000,000 ZEC threshold, but not toward the
+majority.
+
+Nothing else about coinholder voting changes. Ballots are still weighted by
+ZEC, and a simple majority of the ZEC voted for or against still decides the
+result. The ZIP has no privacy implications.
+
+A companion draft [^draft-human-minimum] would add a minimum number of
+distinct human participants. The two can be adopted separately or together.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 1016 requires a minimum of 420,000 ZEC (2% of the total eventual supply)
+to be voted, with a simple majority cast in favor, for a grant proposal to be
+approved [^zip-1016-disbursement]. ZIP 1016 itself lists "Is 420,000 ZEC the
+right threshold for coinholder votes?" as an open question
+[^zip-1016-open-questions].
+
+The threshold counts coins, not people. As of late 2026, at least two single
+holders control a large share of it:
+
+| Holder | ZEC held | Share of the 420,000 ZEC threshold | Share of 1,000,000 ZEC |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Grayscale Zcash ETF (ZCSH) | ~594,293 ZEC (2026-10-30) [^grayscale] | 141% | 59% |
+| Cypherpunk Technologies (Nasdaq: CYPH) | ~326,417 ZEC (2026-09-30) [^blockworks-q3] | 78% | 33% |
+
+Under the current rule, one holder could supply the whole turnout of a
+coinholder-amount voting round, and a vote in which no one else took part
+would still be valid. The author does not claim that either entity has voted,
+or would vote, in this way. The concern is that the rules allow it, so a
+passing result cannot by itself show that coinholders in general, rather than
+one balance sheet, supported a grant.
+
+Raising the threshold to 1,000,000 ZEC puts it well above the largest known
+single holding, and above the two largest combined. Recent high-interest
+rounds have drawn far more than that: the top proposal in the Q3 2026 round
+had about 2.18 million ZEC voted, worth about US$3.1 billion at the time
+[^blockworks-q3]. The change should not stop well-supported proposals from
+passing.
+
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+This ZIP has no privacy implications. It changes a number in ZIP 1016 and
+states how abstentions are counted. It does not change how ballots are cast,
+what voters reveal, or what is published about them.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+* No single holder of ZEC, as currently known, can satisfy the threshold of a
+  coinholder-amount voting round alone.
+* Voters and applicants can know the threshold in advance without any further
+  calculation.
+* The way abstentions are counted is stated, not left to each round's
+  organizers.
+
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+* This ZIP does not change how ballots are weighted.
+* This ZIP does not add a minimum number of human participants. That is left
+  to a companion draft [^draft-human-minimum].
+* This ZIP does not change the veto process of ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016-veto], the
+  funding streams, or the membership of the Key-Holder Organizations.
+* This ZIP does not set a minimum holding for individual voters.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Changes to the ZEC threshold
+
+In the "Disbursement process" section of ZIP 1016 [^zip-1016-disbursement],
+the paragraph beginning "For coinholder votes, a minimum of 420,000 ZEC" is
+amended by replacing "420,000 ZEC (2% of the total eventual supply)" with
+"1,000,000 ZEC". The rest of that paragraph, including the rules for competing
+proposals, is unchanged.
+
+## Counting ZEC voted
+
+For the purpose of the threshold:
+
+* ZEC committed by ballots that approve, reject, or abstain all counts toward
+  ZEC voted.
+* The simple majority is computed over ZEC committed by ballots that approve
+  or reject. Abstaining ZEC does not count in favor or against.
+* ZEC voted is measured on each question separately. Ballots cast on a
+  different proposal, including a competing proposal, do not count.
+
+The Key-Holder Organizations MUST report, for each question, the ZEC voted,
+the ZEC in favor, the ZEC against, and the ZEC abstaining when they publish
+the result of a coinholder-amount voting round.
+
+## Testnet
+
+In the "Testnet-specific considerations" section of ZIP 1016, "The threshold
+of 420,000 ZEC" is replaced with "The threshold of 1,000,000 ZEC".
+
+## Open question removed from ZIP 1016
+
+The open question "Is 420,000 ZEC the right threshold for coinholder votes?"
+is removed from ZIP 1016.
+
+## Activation
+
+This ZIP applies to any coinholder-amount voting round whose voting window
+opens on or after the date this ZIP's Status becomes Active. The Key-Holder
+Organizations SHOULD announce the new threshold when they announce the first
+round to which it applies.
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Why 1,000,000 ZEC
+
+1,000,000 ZEC is about 4.76% of the eventual supply of 21,000,000 ZEC. It is
+well above the largest publicly known single holding (the Grayscale Zcash ETF,
+at about 594,293 ZEC on 2026-10-30 [^grayscale]), and above the two largest
+known holdings combined (about 920,710 ZEC). It is still well below the
+turnout of recent high-interest rounds: the top proposal in the Q3 2026 round
+had about 2.18 million ZEC voted [^blockworks-q3], worth about US$3.1 billion
+at the price of ZEC on 30 September 2026. The new threshold is less than half
+of that turnout.
+
+Turnout in the Q1 2026 round peaked near 500,000 ZEC, so some past proposals
+that passed would not have reached the new threshold. This is intended.
+
+## Why a fixed number
+
+A fixed number was chosen over a percentage of circulating supply so that
+voters and applicants know the threshold in advance. Holdings change, and
+1,000,000 ZEC will not stay above the largest single holding forever. A minimum
+number of human participants, as proposed in the companion draft
+[^draft-human-minimum], is the more durable protection, but it needs a
+proof-of-personhood process that does not exist yet. This ZIP can be adopted
+now, without waiting for that.
+
+## Why abstentions count toward the threshold
+
+Recent rounds have reported abstentions, but ZIP 1016 never said how they
+count. Counting them toward turnout, but not toward the majority, treats an
+abstaining voter as someone who took part without taking a side. The
+alternative, excluding them, would make it harder for a well-attended but
+divided vote to be valid.
+
+
+# Open questions
+
+* Should ZEC that abstains count toward the 1,000,000 ZEC threshold? This draft
+  says yes.
+* Should the threshold be reviewed on a schedule, for example whenever a
+  single known holding passes 80% of it?
+* Is 1,000,000 ZEC too high for routine grant rounds with lower turnout? An
+  alternative is 600,000 ZEC, just above the largest known single holding.
+* This draft sets a minimum total of ZEC voted on a question. It does not set
+  a minimum holding for an individual voter. Should it?
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14, "RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels" and "RFC 8174: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words"](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol-networks]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, Version 2026.8.0 [NU6.3]. Section 3.12: Mainnet and Testnet](protocol/protocol.pdf#networks)
+
+[^zip-1016]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model](zip-1016.md)
+
+[^zip-1016-disbursement]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model, Disbursement process](zip-1016.md#disbursement-process)
+
+[^zip-1016-veto]: [ZIP 1016: Community and Coinholder Funding Model, Veto process](zip-1016.md#veto-process)
+

+This ZIP proposes an encoding for V7 Zcash transactions that reduces the
+impact of future transaction format changes on wallets and other clients.
+Previous format changes required clients to update their parsers even when
+they did not use newly introduced protocol features.
+
+The format defines typecode-length-value encodings for protocol bundles and
+a value pool delta map describing each bundle's effect on the transparent
+transaction value pool for each asset. The entries of this map serve the
+same purpose as the Sapling and Orchard value balance fields have done in
+the past. Effecting data and authorizing data are encoded separately, allowing
+authorizing data to be pruned without removing the transaction's effects.
+
+Clients can parse the common transaction envelope and enumerate public value
+flows without understanding every bundle type or variant. Computing the
+transaction identifier additionally requires a supplied digest for each
+unsupported effecting bundle. This does not eliminate the need to update
+wallets for consensus changes that alter how they must construct or interpret
+transactions.
+
+Future additive bundle introductions can avoid making wallets' support for
+unused features distinguishable on-chain, reducing the need for further
+transaction-format changes and their associated privacy leakage.

+A transaction contains two kinds of information:

+* Changes enacted on global chain state. These belong in effecting bundles,
+  including changes that move no value (such as the potential key rotation
+  bundle in ZIP 270). Together with the value pool delta and authorizing data

+* Constraints on when the state change may be enacted. Pool-specific constraints

+Shielded balancing values
+`````````````````````````
+
+The logical Sapling, Orchard, and Ironwood balancing values are signed integers
+measured in zatoshis, as defined in the 'Balance and Binding Signature' sections
+of the protocol specification. [#protocol-saplingbalance]_ [#protocol-orchardbalance]_
+They are obtained from the V7 encoding as follows:
+
+.. math::
+
+   \begin{aligned}
+   \mathsf{v}^{\textit{SaplingPoolBalance}} &= \mathsf{mValuePoolDeltas}[(\mathsf{SaplingBundleId}, \mathsf{Zec})] \\
+   \mathsf{v}^{\textit{OrchardPoolBalance}} &= \mathsf{mValuePoolDeltas}[(\mathsf{OrchardBundleId}, \mathsf{Zec})] \\
+   \mathsf{v}^{\textit{IronwoodPoolBalance}} &= \mathsf{mValuePoolDeltas}[(\mathsf{IronwoodBundleId}, \mathsf{Zec})]
+   \end{aligned}

+Each balancing value has the sign convention defined for its pool: a positive
+value takes net value from the corresponding chain value pool and adds it to the
+transparent transaction value pool; a negative value does the reverse.

+* $\mathtt{nActionsOrchard}$ and $\mathtt{nActionsIronwood}$ are the

+* $\mathtt{enableSpendsOrchard}$ and $\mathtt{enableOutputsOrchard}$ are the

prs.title: Draft ZIP: Increase the block size limit to 3 MB
prs.author: evan-forbes
prs.bodyExcerpt: This draft ZIP increases the serialized block size limit from 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 bytes in a network upgrade after NU7. It preserves shielded action limits, the transaction-size cap, and signature-operation limits. Block target spacing remains a separate proposal. The draft specifies activation b

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,316 @@
+
+    ZIP: Unassigned
+    Title: Increase the Block Size Limit to 3 MB
+    Owners: Dev Ojha <dev@valargroup.dev>
+            Evan Forbes <evan@valargroup.dev>
+    Status: Draft
+    Category: Consensus
+    Created: 2026-11-06
+    License: MIT
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", and "SHOULD" in this document are to be
+interpreted as described in BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, they appear
+in all capitals.
+
+The terms "block chain", "consensus branch", and "network upgrade" follow
+ZIP 200. [^zip-0200] Block and transaction encodings follow the Zcash Protocol
+Specification. [^protocol]
+
+MB means 1,000,000 bytes. The existing block
+size limit is 2 MB; this proposal increases it to 3 MB.
+
+"Orphan rate" means distinct observed orphan blocks divided by the sum of
+canonical and observed orphan blocks. Here, an orphan block is a block outside
+the final agreed chain. The experiment below counts a block
+only if at least one node recorded a successful commit. It does not count
+every solved block that a miner discarded before submission.
+
+"Reach 90%" means elapsed time from the miner's solution-ready event to
+decoded block availability at 72 of the experiment's 80 nodes, including
+the originating node at time zero.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This proposal increases the block size limit from 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 bytes
+(3 MB) in a network upgrade after NU7. It preserves ZIP 218's shielded action
+limits and shared shielded budget. [^zip-0218] It also preserves the
+2,000,000-byte transaction cap currently enforced by consensus and the existing signature-operation
+limit.
+
+The additional space primarily increases capacity for transparent
+transactions. It prepares the block byte budget for future shielded
+throughput without raising today's shielded scanning burden through an
+action-limit increase. A future proposal to increase shielded action limits
+would depend on adoption and operational validation of private information
+retrieval (PIR), with measured wallet bandwidth and privacy costs.
+
+The proposal also changes block-message size negotiation so that upgraded
+peers can relay valid 3 MB blocks. It leaves block target spacing to separate
+proposals. Larger blocks increase full-node bandwidth, storage, and
+potential validation work.
+
+
+# Motivation
+
+ZIP 218 separates the block byte budget from the shielded action budget.
+The byte budget limits serialized data; the action budget limits shielded
+work and compact sync bandwidth. Its action limits do not apply to the
+transparent components of transactions. [^zip-0218]
+
+With the upcoming Tachyon shielded pool, wallets are intended to use more
+scalable flows, such as out-of-band communication and PIR, to discover
+incoming transactions. Given that, the limiters on the throughput of Zcash
+will be off-chain services and the throughput of consensus itself.
+Increasing the throughput of consensus necessitates increasing the block
+size, lowering the average block time, or both. Under single-chain proof of
+work, it is hard to reduce block times too far because of their high
+variance, hence it is critical to take on the trade-off of larger block
+sizes.
+
+Increasing the byte budget now allows more transparent transactions when
+bytes are the binding constraint. Increasing transparent throughput is an
+intermediate benefit, not Zcash's long-term scaling objective. Deploying
+and measuring larger blocks also prepares the network for future shielded
+throughput once wallets can handle it privately and efficiently.
+
+This proposal separates those decisions. It increases block space while
+retaining all shielded action limits. PIR adoption does not automatically
+activate higher limits; any change requires a separate consensus proposal.
+
+
+# Requirements
+
+- Increase the maximum serialized block size to exactly 3 MB.
+- Preserve historical validity and all existing shielded action limits.
+- Preserve transaction-size, signature-operation, and script limits.
+- Support full-sized blocks through relay, synchronization, and mining.
+- Bound resource use before accepting untrusted block bodies.
+
+
+# Specification
+
+## Activation and block size
+
+Define the following constants:
+
+$$\mathsf{ThreeMBActivationHeight} : \mathbb{N}.$$
+
+$$\mathsf{ThreeMBBlockSizeLimit} : \mathbb{N} := 3\times10^6 = 3{,}000{,}000.$$
+
+A deployment ZIP will assign $\mathsf{ThreeMBActivationHeight}$ for each
+network. It MUST be greater than that network's NU7 activation height.
+Let $A = \mathsf{ThreeMBActivationHeight}$. For block height
+$h \in \mathbb{N}$, define:
+
+$$\mathsf{BlockSizeLimit}(h) := \begin{cases}2{,}000{,}000 & h < A,\\3{,}000{,}000 & h \geq A.\end{cases}$$
+
+Replace the fixed block size bound in § 7.6 'Block Header Encoding and
+Consensus' with the requirement that a block at height $h$ MUST have encoded
+size at most $\mathsf{BlockSizeLimit}(h)$. [^protocol-blockheader]
+
+In the same section, qualify the comparison with Bitcoin's block size limit:
+Zcash's 2,000,000-byte limit applies below $A$; the 3,000,000-byte limit applies
+at or above $A$.
+
+In ZIP 218's specification, replace the statement that the overall 2 MB block
+size limit continues to apply with a reference to $\mathsf{BlockSizeLimit}(h)$
+after this proposal activates. ZIP 218's shielded action limits remain
+unchanged. [^zip-0218]
+
+Encoded size includes the block header, its Equihash solution, the encoded
+transaction count, and every transaction, including the coinbase. It excludes
+the 24-byte P2P message header and storage or RPC wrappers. No field receives
+a size discount.
+
+Validators MUST select the limit using the candidate block's height on its
+parent chain. The local tip height and the peer's advertised height MUST NOT
+determine consensus validity. Validators MUST retain the old limit below
+$A$, including during initial synchronization, side-chain validation, and
+reorganizations across activation.
+
+## Transaction and computational limits
+
+Define $\mathsf{TransactionSizeLimit} : \mathbb{N} := 2{,}000{,}000$ bytes.
+For every block at or above $A$, each transaction, including the coinbase,
+MUST have encoded size at most $\mathsf{TransactionSizeLimit}$.
+Pre-activation transaction rules remain unchanged.
+
+The transaction bound remains independent of the block bound. The additional
+space admits more transactions. zcashd already enforces an explicit
+2,000,000-byte transaction cap. The protocol specification states a
+100,000-byte cap before Sapling; after Sapling, the block envelope also
+limits the size of any included transaction. This proposal makes the
+independent 2,000,000-byte post-activation transaction cap explicit, so
+increasing the block envelope does not admit larger individual transactions.
+[^zcashd-limits] [^protocol]
+
+The block signature-operation limit remains 20,000, using the existing
+counting rules, including P2SH signature operations. Existing script limits
+and transaction-format bounds remain unchanged. [^zcashd-limits]
+
+This proposal does not change block target spacing, but benchmarks for safety
+are done with 20-second target spacing in mind.
+
+## Block relay and message framing
+
+ZIP 204 currently limits each message payload to 2,097,152 bytes. That limit
+cannot carry a valid 3 MB block. Amend its 'Maximum Message Size' rules as
+follows. [^zip-0204]
+
+Define $\mathsf{ThreeMBProtocolVersion} : \mathbb{N}$, to be assigned by the
+deployment ZIP. For a connection whose negotiated protocol version is at
+least this value, the maximum `block` message payload is 3,000,000 bytes.
+For older negotiated versions, retain the 2,097,152-byte maximum. Other
+commands retain their existing payload and item-count limits.
+
+Nodes MUST reject a declared payload length above the applicable maximum
+before allocating a buffer for that payload. A decoder MUST consume exactly
+one block from a `block` payload and reject trailing data, truncated fields,
+and invalid encodings. Existing checksum checks remain in force.
+
+Upgraded nodes MUST support the larger `block` payload on upgraded
+connections even when their local tip is below $A$. They still apply the
+height-dependent consensus bound when validating the block. This permits
+initial synchronization and out-of-order delivery across activation without
+accepting oversized pre-activation blocks.
+
+Senders MUST NOT send a payload above the peer connection's negotiated
+maximum. The deployment MUST update minimum peer versions and apply
+ZIP 201's upgrade peer-management rules so that upgraded nodes can retain
+compatible peers at activation. [^zip-0201]
+
+## Mining and node interfaces
+
+`getblocktemplate` MUST report `sizelimit` for the candidate height, normally
+one above the selected parent. Template selection MUST reserve space for
+the complete header, encoded transaction count, and completed coinbase.
+Miners MUST re-evaluate the limit when a parent change crosses activation.
+
+Block submission and retrieval interfaces MUST support every otherwise-valid
+block within the applicable limit. This includes proposal validation, RPC
+submission, historical retrieval, and local block import.
+
+Deserializers MUST distinguish the block envelope limit from transaction
+and field limits. Increasing the block limit MUST NOT implicitly increase
+`tx`, inventory, address, or header-message limits. Nodes SHOULD bound
+aggregate queued block bytes and decoded memory, rather than relying only
+on a count of blocks or connections.
+
+This proposal does not increase mempool memory defaults or change ZIP 317's
+fee calculation. ZIP 401's cost limit remains a node resource policy, not a
+fixed entitlement to a number of full blocks. [^zip-0317] [^zip-0401]
+
+
+# Rationale
+
+## Choice of block size
+
+The authors chose 3 MB because, at that size, current Zakura and Zebra Andale
+implementations keep orphan rates below Ethereum's historical average of
+5.4%. The experiment below provides preliminary Zakura evidence near that size.
+
+## Throughput and resource costs
+
+The new byte budget is $3{,}000{,}000/2{,}000{,}000 = 1.5$ times the old
+budget, an increase of 50%. Transaction throughput depends
+on the workload. Transparent transactions can use the additional space,
+but signature operations, script execution, and UTXO access can become
+binding constraints. Action-limited shielded workloads do not receive a
+corresponding increase in transactions per block.
+
+The following bounds assume every canonical block reaches 3 MB and blocks
+arrive at the stated target spacing:
+
+| Target spacing | Raw block payload rate | Raw block data per day | Capacity relative to 2 MB at 25 seconds |
+|----------------|------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|
+| 25 seconds | 120,000 bytes/second | 10.368 GB | 1.5× |
+| 20 seconds | 150,000 bytes/second | 12.96 GB | 1.875× |
+
+These figures exclude repeated relay, orphan blocks, transport overhead,
+indexes, and state growth. They describe full-block traffic, not light-wallet
+compact sync. Disk and memory costs can grow differently from serialized
+bytes, especially for blocks with many small transparent outputs.
+
+Keeping the 20,000 signature-operation limit bounds counted operations; it
+does not bound all validation work. Transparent-heavy blocks require
+measurements of script execution, UTXO reads and writes, memory, and
+validation-to-mining-tip latency.
+
+## Propagation experiment
+
+A November 2026 private-network experiment used 80 Zakura nodes across 12
+regions at a 20-second target spacing. Blocks filled twice ZIP 218's normal
+shielded action limit: 660 Ironwood actions. The measured blocks occupied
+3,026,379 bytes, approximately 3 MB and slightly above the proposed limit.
+
+| Measurement | Mean | Median | 95th percentile |
+|-------------|------|--------|-----------------|
+| Block propagation to 90% of nodes | 1.20 s | 1.02 s | 2.18 s |
+
+The observed orphan rate was **3.6%**.
+
+**TODO:** Report propagation to 90% of nodes using a mixed Zakura / Zebra Andale
+network.
+
+
+## Computation and I/O benchmarks
+
+The original Zcash block-size increase prompted analysis of verification
+costs across different input/output mixes. [^zcashd-worst-case] A fixed
+signature-operation limit does not capture every validation cost.
+
+Before deployment, benchmark the following workloads at the proposed limit:
+
+| Workload | Costs to examine |
+|----------|------------------|
+| Many small transparent transactions | Per-transaction overhead and UTXO lookups |
+| Output-heavy transparent transactions | UTXO growth and database writes |
+| Signature-heavy transparent transactions | Signature verification and script execution |
+| Mixed transparent and shielded transactions | Combined UTXO and proof-verification work under unchanged action limits |
+
+For each workload, report validation-to-mining-tip time, UTXO reads and writes,
+and peak memory. Record client version, hardware, and cache conditions so
+others can reproduce the results.
+
+
+# Deployment
+
+Deploy through a network upgrade after NU7. A deployment ZIP will assign
+activation heights, consensus branch IDs, and the new protocol version.
+This proposal can activate with a separately specified spacing change, but
+does not require a 20-second target.
+
+Before advancing to Proposed status, publish reproducible experiment inputs
+and resolve the deployment assignments. Validate the byte and computational
+boundaries across independent clients. Run matched 3 MB transparent and
+mixed workloads at the selected spacing, including constrained bandwidth,
+propagation tails, orphan blocks, UTXO growth, and mining-tip adoption.
+
+
+# References
+
+[^BCP14]: [Information on BCP 14](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp14)
+
+[^protocol]: [Zcash Protocol Specification](protocol/protocol.pdf)
+
+[^protocol-blockheader]: [Zcash Protocol Specification, § 7.6: Block Header Encoding and Consensus](protocol/protocol.pdf#blockheader)
+
+[^zip-0200]: [ZIP 200: Network Upgrade Mechanism](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0200)
+
+[^zip-0201]: [ZIP 201: Network Peer Management for Overwinter](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0201)
+
+[^zip-0204]: [ZIP 204: Zcash P2P Network Protocol](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0204)
+
+[^zip-0218]: [ZIP 218: 25-second Block Target Spacing](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0218)
+
+[^zip-0317]: [ZIP 317: Proportional Transfer Fee Mechanism](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0317)
+
+[^zip-0401]: [ZIP 401: Addressing Mempool Denial-of-Service](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0401)
+
+[^zcashd-limits]: [zcashd: consensus limits](https://github.com/zcash/zcash/blob/master/src/consensus/consensus.h)
+
+[^zcashd-worst-case]: [zcashd issue #1077: Worst-case block verification costs](https://github.com/zcash/zcash/issues/1077)
